metadata.title: Translation invariant pure state on $\otimes_{\IZ}\!M_d(\IC)$ and Haag duality

extraction_notes.note: Theorem 2.1 is introduced as a recalled result (Theorem 5.1 of [BJKW], after Popescu), while the introduction calls it a finer version and a new feature; marked origin external with its proof as paper.

Cross-references in words are often misnumbered ("Theorem 2.4" for Proposition 2.4, "Theorem 3.4/3.5" for Propositions 3.4/3.5, "Theorem 2.6 (a)" in the proof of Theorem 1.1); edges point to the intended results. The paper has no \label/\ref at all, so every dependency edge was added by hand.
Equation (23) $v_k=PS_kP$ also occurs verbatim in earlier text, so the finishing step could not match it to its fact and its number is not filled.
definition or open_problem: phrased as 'one interesting problem ... how to describe ${\mathcal I}$', but its role is to introduce ${\mathcal I}$, which later results use.
The introduction's statement of BJKW Lemma 7.4 (adds 'factor iff $\omega_R$ factor') was recorded in also_stated_at of Proposition 2.6 rather than as a separate node.

Historical and motivational asides (Accardi's KMS result, the Mackey imprimitivity statement for e_n, failure of the converse of Kolmogorov implies purity, one-line remarks such as 'Thus M-tilde is contained in M''') were not made nodes.

nodes.name: Factor state
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em A state $\omega$ on a $C^*$-algebra ${\mathcal B}$ is called a factor if the center of the von-Neumann algebra $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B})''$ is trivial, where $({\mathcal H}_{\omega},\pi_{\omega},\Omega)$ is the GNS space associated with $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ [BR vol-I].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Pure state
nodes.statement: A state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ is called pure if $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B})''={\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}_{\omega})$, the algebra of all bounded operators on ${\mathcal H}_{\omega}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: UHF algebra over Z^k
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let ${\mathcal B}=\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}^k} \!M_d(\mathbb{C})$ be the uniformly hyper-finite $C^*$-algebra over the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^k$ of dimension $k \ge 1$, where $\!M_d(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of $d \times d$-matrices over the field of complex number $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation invariant state on Z^k lattice
nodes.statement: A state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ is called translation invariant if $\omega(x)=\omega(\theta_{\bar{m}}(x))$ where $\bar{m}=(m_1,m_2,.,m_k)$ and $\theta_{\bar{m}}$ is the translation induced by $\bar{\mathbb{Z}} \rightarrow \bar{\mathbb{Z}} + \bar{m}$ for all $\bar{z} \in \mathbb{Z}^k$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Powers' criterion for translation invariant factor states
nodes.statement: It is well known since late 60's [Pow] that a translation invariant state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ is a factor state if and only if \begin{equation} \mbox{sup}_{x \in {\mathcal B}_{\Lambda_n^c}, ||x|| \le 1}|\omega(xy)) - \omega(x)\omega(y)| \rightarrow 0 \end{equation} for all $y \in {\mathcal B}$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$, where $\Lambda_{n}$ is the local algebra with support in the finite set $\{\bar{m}: -n \le m_k \le n \}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: A translation invariant state is a factor state iff correlations with far-away observables asymptotically factorize.
assumptions: a translation invariant state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$
conclusions: is a factor state if and only if

nodes.name: Equation (1)
nodes.statement: \mbox{sup}_{x \in {\mathcal B}_{\Lambda_n^c}, ||x|| \le 1}|\omega(xy)) - \omega(x)\omega(y)| \rightarrow 0
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Quantum spin chain algebra B
nodes.statement: The quantum spin chain that we consider here is described by a $\mbox{UHF}$ $C^*$-algebra denoted by ${\mathcal B}=\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}M_d(\mathbb{C})$. Here ${\mathcal B}$ is the $C^*$ -completion of the infinite tensor product of the algebra $M_d(\mathbb{C})$ of $d \times d$ complex matrices [Sa], each component of the tensor product element is indexed by an integer $j$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local copy Q^(j)
nodes.statement: Let $Q$ be a matrix in $M_d(\mathbb{C})$. We denote the element $Q^{(j)}=...\otimes 1 \otimes 1 ... 1 \otimes Q \otimes 1 \otimes ... 1\otimes ,,. $, where $Q$ appears in the $j$-th component.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local algebra B_Lambda
nodes.statement: Given a subset $\Lambda$ of $\mathbb{Z}$, ${\mathcal B}_{\Lambda}$ is defined as the $C^*$-sub-algebra of ${\mathcal B}$ generated by all $Q^{(j)}$ with $Q \in {\bf M}_d(\mathbb{C})$, $j \in \Lambda$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local algebra B_loc
nodes.statement: We also set $${\mathcal B}_{loc}= \bigcup_{\Lambda:|\Lambda| < \infty } {\mathcal B}_{\Lambda}$$ where $|\Lambda|$ is the cardinality of $\Lambda$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Restriction omega_Lambda
nodes.statement: The restriction of $\omega$ to ${\mathcal B}_{\Lambda}$ is denoted by $\omega_{\Lambda}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Half-chain restrictions omega_R and omega_L
nodes.statement: We also set $\omega_{R}=\omega_{[1,\infty)}$ and $\omega_{L}= \omega_{(-\infty,0]}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation automorphism theta_k
nodes.statement: The translation $\theta_k$ is an automorphism of ${\mathcal B}$ defined by $\theta_k(Q^{(j)})=Q^{(j+k)}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation invariant state
nodes.statement: We say $\omega$ is translation invariant if $\omega \circ \theta_k = \omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ ( $\omega \circ \theta_1 = \omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ ).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation invariant Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We will consider a Hamiltonian in one dimensional lattice of the following form \begin{equation} H= \sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} \theta^k(h_0) \end{equation} for $h^*_0=h_0 \in {\mathcal B}_{loc}$ where the formal sum gives an auto-morphism $\alpha=(\alpha_t:t \in \mathbb{R})$ via the thermodynamic limit of $\alpha^{\Lambda}_t(x)=e^{itH_{\Lambda}}xe^{-itH_{\Lambda}}$ for a net of finite subsets of the lattice $\Lambda \uparrow \mathbb{Z}$ whose surface energies are uniformly bounded, where $H_{\Lambda}=\sum_{k \in \Lambda} \theta^k(h_0)$ [Ru,BR2].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Formal translation invariant Hamiltonian $H=\sum_k\theta^k(h_0)$ whose dynamics is the thermodynamic limit of local ones.

nodes.name: Equation (2)
nodes.statement: H= \sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} \theta^k(h_0)
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Cuntz algebra O_d
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em First we recall that the Cuntz algebra ${\mathcal O}_d ( d \in \{2,3,.., \} )$ [Cun] is the universal unital $C^*$-algebra generated by the elements $\{s_1,s_2,..., s_d \}$ subject to the following Cuntz relations: \begin{equation} s^*_is_j=\delta^i_j1,\;\;\sum_{1 \le i \le d } s_is^*_i=1 \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: s^*_is_j=\delta^i_j1,\;\;\sum_{1 \le i \le d } s_is^*_i=1
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Canonical U(d) action on O_d
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em There is a canonical action of the group $U(d)$ of unitary $d \times d$ matrices on ${\mathcal O}_d$ given by $$\beta_g(s_i)=\sum_{1 \le j \le d}\overline{g^j_i}s_j$$ for $g=(g^i_j) \in U(d)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Gauge action
nodes.statement: In particular the gauge action is defined by $$\beta_z(s_i)=zs_i,\;\;z \in I\!\!T =S^1= \{z \in \mathbb{C}: |z|=1 \}.$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: UHF_d as gauge-fixed subalgebra
nodes.statement: If UHF$_d$ is the fixed point sub-algebra under the gauge action, then UHF$_d$ is the closure of the linear span of all Wick ordered monomials of the form $$s_{i_1}...s_{i_k}s^*_{j_k}...s^*_{j_1}$$ which is also isomorphic to the UHF$_d$ algebra $${\mathcal B}_R =\otimes^{\infty}_1M_d(\mathbb{C})$$ so that the isomorphism carries the Wick ordered monomial above into the matrix element $$e^{i_1}_{j_1}(1)\otimes e^{i_2}_{j_2}(2) \otimes....\otimes e^{i_k}_{j_k}(k) \otimes 1 \otimes 1 ....$$ and the restriction of $\beta_g$ to $UHF_d$ is then carried to action $$Ad(g)\otimes Ad(g) \otimes Ad(g) \otimes ....$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: UHF$_d$, the gauge-fixed subalgebra of ${\mathcal O}_d$, is identified with $\otimes_1^\infty M_d$.

nodes.name: Canonical endomorphism lambda
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We also define the canonical endomorphism $\lambda$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ by \begin{equation} \lambda(x)=\sum_{1 \le i \le d}s_ixs^*_i \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (4)
nodes.statement: \lambda(x)=\sum_{1 \le i \le d}s_ixs^*_i
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Index set of finite sequences
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let $d \in \{2,3,..,,..\}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_d$ be a set of $d$ elements. ${\mathcal I}$ be the set of finite sequences $I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_m)$ where $i_k \in \mathbb{Z}_d$ and $m \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Multi-index monomials s_I
nodes.statement: We also include empty set $\emptyset \in {\mathcal I}$ and set $s_{\emptyset }=1=s^*_{\emptyset}$, $s_{I}=s_{i_1}......s_{i_m} \in {\mathcal O}_d $ and $s^*_{I}=s^*_{i_m}...s^*_{i_1} \in {\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Set K_omega of lambda-invariant extensions
nodes.statement: Using weak$^*$ compactness of the convex set of states on a $C^*$-algebra, a standard averaging method ensures that the set $$K_{\omega}=\{ \psi \in {\mathcal S}({\mathcal O}_d): \psi \lambda= \psi,\; \psi_| \mbox{UHF}_d = \omega_R \}$$ is a non-empty compact subset of ${\mathcal S}({\mathcal O}_d)$, where ${\mathcal S}({\mathcal O}_d)$ is the weak$^*$ compact convex set of states on ${\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: GNS space of psi
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Irrespective of the factor property of $\omega$, we may choose an element $\psi$ of $K_{\omega}$ and consider the GNS space $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ associated with state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Support projection P
nodes.statement: We set $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ to be the support projection of $\psi$ i.e. $P=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega]$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Support projection is sub-harmonic
nodes.statement: Invariance property of the state $\psi=\psi \lambda$ will ensure that $P\Lambda(I-P)P=0$ where $$\Lambda(X)=\sum_i S_iXS_i^*$$ is the canonical endomorphism on $\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ with $S_i=\pi_{\psi}(s_i)$. This verifies that \begin{equation} S_i^*P=PS^*_iP,\;1 \le i \le d \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (5)
nodes.statement: S_i^*P=PS^*_iP,\;1 \le i \le d
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Popescu elements v_i on the support
nodes.statement: We define a family of contractions $\{v_i:1 \le i \le d\}$ in ${\mathcal M}$ by $v_i=PS_iP,1 \le i \le d $ where we set von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}=P\pi_{\phi}({\mathcal O}_d)''P$ acting on Hilbert subspace ${\mathcal K}$ where ${\mathcal K}$ is range of $P$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Reduced Markov map tau
nodes.statement: Thus we get ${\mathcal M} = \{v_i: 1 \le i \le d \}''$ and a unital completely positive map $\tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P=\sum_iv_ixv_i^*$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Fixed points of tau equal the commutant
nodes.statement: Furthermore a crucial point to be noted that the support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ being equal to $P$, by our construction we have \begin{equation} \{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_i v_ixv_i^* = x \}= {\mathcal M}' \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (6)
nodes.statement: \{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_i v_ixv_i^* = x \}= {\mathcal M}'
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Popescu's elements
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Conversely let ${\mathcal M}$ be a von-Neumann algebra acting on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$. A family of contractions $\{v_i:1 \le i \le d \}$ in ${\mathcal M}$ is called Popescu's elements if $\sum_iv_iv_i^*=1$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: State psi induced by a Popescu system
nodes.statement: For a faithful normal state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ we define state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ by \begin{equation} \psi(s_Is_J^*)=\phi(v_Iv_J^*) \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (7)
nodes.statement: \psi(s_Is_J^*)=\phi(v_Iv_J^*)
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: omega_R in terms of Popescu elements
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We verify also with $v_i^*=PS^*_iP$ that \begin{equation} \omega_R(|e_{i_1}><e_{j_1}| \otimes |e_{i_2}><e_{j_2}| \otimes ...\otimes |e_{i_n}><e_{j_n}|)= \phi(v_Iv_J^*) \end{equation} where $v_I=v_{i_n}...v_{i_2}v_{i_1}$ and $v^*_J=v_{j_1}^*v^*_{j_2}...v^*_{j_n}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (8)
nodes.statement: \omega_R(|e_{i_1}><e_{j_1}| \otimes |e_{i_2}><e_{j_2}| \otimes ...\otimes |e_{i_n}><e_{j_n}|)= \phi(v_Iv_J^*)
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Completely positive map I!E
nodes.statement: Let $V^*:{\mathcal K} \rightarrow {\mathcal K} \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$ be an isometry and in an orthonormal basis $(e_i)$ for $\mathbb{C}^d$, we have $V^*=(v_1^*,v_2^*,..,v_d^*)$ with $v_i \in {\mathcal M}$. We define $$I\!\!E: \!M_d({\mathcal M}) \rightarrow {\mathcal M}$$ by $$I\!\!E(X)=VXV^*=\sum_{1 \le i,j \le d} v_ix^i_jv_j^* $$ where $X=((x^i_j))$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Maps I!E_A
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ be a state on ${\mathcal M}$ such that $$\phi(I\!\!E(B \otimes I_d))=\phi(B),\;\forall B \in {\mathcal M} $$ For each $A \in M_d(\mathbb{C})$, define $I\!\!E_{A}:{\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal M}$ by $$B \rightarrow I\!\!E(B \otimes A)$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Quantum Markov state formula defines a translation invariant state
nodes.statement: Then \begin{equation} \omega(A_1 \otimes A_1 \otimes A_3 ...\otimes A_m)=\phi(I\!\!E_{A_1} \circ I\!\!E_{A_2} \circ ..I\!\!E_{A_m}(I_{{\mathcal K}})) \end{equation} defines a $\lambda$-invariant state on ${\mathcal B}_R$ and the inductive limit state of ${\mathcal B}_R \rightarrow ^{\lambda} {\mathcal B}_R$ [Sa] gives a translation invariant state on ${\mathcal B}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (9)
nodes.statement: \omega(A_1 \otimes A_1 \otimes A_3 ...\otimes A_m)=\phi(I\!\!E_{A_1} \circ I\!\!E_{A_2} \circ ..I\!\!E_{A_m}(I_{{\mathcal K}}))
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Markov map
nodes.statement: $I\!\!E$ naturally gives a Markov map i.e. a unital completely positive map on ${\mathcal M}$ defined by $\tau(x)=I\!\!E( x \otimes I_d)=\sum_i v_ixv_i^*$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Existence of the dual Markov map
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em The state $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x \Omega>$ on ${\mathcal M}$ being faithful and invariant of $\tau:{\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal M}$ we find a unique unital completely positive map $\tilde{\tau}:{\mathcal M}' \rightarrow {\mathcal M}'$ satisfying the duality relation \begin{equation} <y\Omega,\tau(x)\Omega>= <\tilde{\tau}(y)\Omega,x\Omega> \end{equation} for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$ and $y \in {\mathcal M}'$, where ${\mathcal M}'$ is the commutant of ${\mathcal M}$ in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal H})$. For a proof we refer to section 8 in the monograph [OP] or [Mo1].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: A faithful $\tau$-invariant state yields a unique ucp dual map $\tilde\tau$ on ${\mathcal M}'$.

nodes.name: Equation (10)
nodes.statement: <y\Omega,\tau(x)\Omega>= <\tilde{\tau}(y)\Omega,x\Omega>
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Modular conjugation and modular operator
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em $\phi$ being also a faithful state, $\Omega \in {\mathcal K}$ is a cyclic and separating vector for ${\mathcal M}$ and the closure of the close-able operator $S_0:x\Omega \rightarrow x^*\Omega, S$ possesses a polar decomposition $S={\mathcal J} \Delta^{1/2}$, where ${\mathcal J}$ is an anti-unitary and $\Delta$ is a non-negative self-adjoint operator on ${\mathcal K}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Tomita's theorem
nodes.statement: Tomita's [BR] theorem says that $\Delta^{it} {\mathcal M} \Delta^{-it}={\mathcal M},\;t \in \mathbb{R}$ and ${\mathcal J} {\mathcal M} {\mathcal J}={\mathcal M}'$, where ${\mathcal M}'$ is the commutant of ${\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Modular automorphism group
nodes.statement: We define the modular automorphism group $\sigma=(\sigma_t,\;t \in I\!\!T )$ on ${\mathcal M}$ by $$\sigma_t(x)=\Delta^{it}x\Delta^{-it}$$ which satisfies the modular relation $$\phi(x\sigma_{-{i \over 2}}(y))=\phi(\sigma_{{i \over 2}}(y)x)$$ for any two analytic elements $x,y$ for the automorphism.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Tomita's conjugation operator and modular automorphisms
nodes.statement: ${\mathcal J}$ and $\sigma=(\sigma_t,\;t \in \mathbb{R})$ are called Tomita's conjugation operator and modular automorphisms associated with $\phi$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual Popescu elements relations (intro)
nodes.statement: By KMS or modular relation [BR vol-I] we verify that $$\sum_k \tilde{v}_k \tilde{v}_k^*=1$$ and \begin{equation} \tilde{\tau}(y)=\sum_k \tilde{v}_ky\tilde{v}^*_k \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \phi(v_Iv^*_J)= \phi(\tilde{v}_{\tilde{I}}\tilde{v}^*_{\tilde{J}}) \end{equation} where $\tilde{I}=(i_n,..,i_2,i_1)$ if $I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_n)$. Moreover $\tilde{v}^*_I\Omega = {\mathcal J} \sigma_{i \over 2}(v_{\tilde{I}})^*{\mathcal J}\Omega= {\mathcal J} \Delta^{1 \over 2}v_{\tilde{I}}\Omega =v^*_{\tilde{I}}\Omega$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: The dual elements $\tilde v_k$ satisfy the Popescu relation, implement $\tilde\tau$, and reproduce $\phi$ with reversed words.

nodes.name: Equation (11)
nodes.statement: \tilde{\tau}(y)=\sum_k \tilde{v}_ky\tilde{v}^*_k
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (12)
nodes.statement: \phi(v_Iv^*_J)= \phi(\tilde{v}_{\tilde{I}}\tilde{v}^*_{\tilde{J}})
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual algebra M-tilde
nodes.statement: We also set $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ to be the von-Neumann algebra generated by $\{\tilde{v}_k: 1 \le k \le d \}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: When do the dual fixed points equal M (equality (13))
nodes.statement: The major problem that we will address in the text when do we have the following equality: \begin{equation} \{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k \tilde{v}_kx\tilde{v}_k^*= x \} ={\mathcal M} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (13)
nodes.statement: \{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k \tilde{v}_kx\tilde{v}_k^*= x \} ={\mathcal M}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equality (13) makes P the support projection of the dual representation
nodes.statement: Equality in (13) will ensure that $P:\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \rightarrow {\mathcal K}$ is also the support projection of $\tilde{\pi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ where $\tilde{\pi}$ is the Popescu's prescription of Stinespring representation $\tilde{\pi}: {\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}})$ associated with the completely positive map $s_Is_J^* \rightarrow \tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}_J^*,\;|I|,|J| < \infty $ so that $P\tilde{\pi}(s^*_i)P=\tilde{\pi}(s_i^*)P=\tilde{v}^*_i$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Correspondence between translation invariant factor states and Popescu elements
nodes.statement: However by Lemma 7.4 in [BJKW] for a factor state $\omega$, if we choose an extreme point $\psi \in K_{\omega}$, two such extreme points $\psi$ and $\psi'$ in $K_{\omega}$ are related by $\psi'=\phi \beta_z$ for some $z \in S^1$, ${\mathcal P}$ is uniquely determined modulo a unitary conjugation. In other words we find a one-one correspondence between \begin{equation} \omega \Leftrightarrow \omega_R \Leftrightarrow K^e_{\omega} \Leftrightarrow {\mathcal P}_e \end{equation} modulo unitary conjugation where $K^e_{\omega}$ denotes the set of extreme points in $K_{\omega}$ and ${\mathcal P}_e$ the set of Popescu's elements associated with extreme points of $K_{\omega}$ on support projection of the state as described above.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: For factor $\omega$, Popescu elements on the support of extremal $\psi\in K_\omega$ determine $\omega$ up to unitary conjugation.

nodes.name: Equation (14)
nodes.statement: \omega \Leftrightarrow \omega_R \Leftrightarrow K^e_{\omega} \Leftrightarrow {\mathcal P}_e
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Ergodic Markov map
nodes.statement: A unital completely positive map $\tau$ on a von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}$ with an invariant normal state $\phi$ [BJKW,Mo1] is called {\it ergodic} if \begin{equation} {1 \over N}\sum_{0 \le k \le N-1}\tau^k(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)I \end{equation} as $N \rightarrow \infty$ in weak$^*$ topology for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (15)
nodes.statement: {1 \over N}\sum_{0 \le k \le N-1}\tau^k(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)I
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Haag duality property
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For a translation invariant factor state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$, we say it admits {\it Haag duality } property if \begin{equation} \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'= \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (16)
nodes.statement: \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'= \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Haag duality implies purity
nodes.statement: It is clear that such a factor state is pure.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Haag duality for translation invariant pure states
nodes.statement: A pure mathematical question that arises here whether converse is true? i.e. Do we always have Haag duality property for a translation invariant pure state of ${\mathcal B}$?
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Haag duality for type-I half-chain restrictions
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em In case $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a type-I factor state, Haag duality property follows easily. In fact we can find Hilbert spaces ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi},\;{\mathcal H}^+_{\pi}$ such that ${\mathcal H}_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi} \otimes {\mathcal H}^+_{\pi}$ so that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'' \equiv {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}) \otimes I_{{\mathcal H}^+_{\pi}}$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \equiv I_{{\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}} \otimes {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^+_{\pi})$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Proof of Haag duality in the type-I case
nodes.statement: A simple proof goes as follows: $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ being a type-I factor, its commutant is also a type-I factor. Thus we have an inclusion of type-I sub-factor $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$. Without loss of generality we assume now that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'={\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$. Now we again use type-I factor property of $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$ to write ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi} \equiv {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1) \otimes {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)$ for two Hilbert spaces ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(k),\; k=1,2$ so that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \equiv {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1)) \otimes I_{{\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)}$. Since $\omega$ is pure we have $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \bigcap \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'=\mathbb{C}$ and so ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)=\mathbb{C}$. Thus we arrive at our conclusion.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Type-I tensor splitting of the commutant; purity forces the leftover tensor factor to be trivial.

nodes.name: Commutant of a type-I factor is type-I; inclusion of type-I factors
nodes.statement: A simple proof goes as follows: $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ being a type-I factor, its commutant is also a type-I factor. Thus we have an inclusion of type-I sub-factor $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Commutant of a type-I factor is type-I; inclusion of type-I factors

nodes.name: Tensor-split the commutant
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality we assume now that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'={\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$. Now we again use type-I factor property of $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$ to write ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi} \equiv {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1) \otimes {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)$ for two Hilbert spaces ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(k),\; k=1,2$ so that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \equiv {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1)) \otimes I_{{\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Tensor-split the commutant

nodes.name: Purity forces the extra factor to be trivial
nodes.statement: Since $\omega$ is pure we have $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \bigcap \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'=\mathbb{C}$ and so ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)=\mathbb{C}$. Thus we arrive at our conclusion.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Purity forces the extra factor to be trivial

nodes.name: Quantum Markov state
nodes.statement: Functional relation (9) is called {\it quantum Marvov state } by Luigi Accardi [Ac] as a generalization of classical Markov state or more generally of a classical Gibbs state.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Finitely correlated state
nodes.statement: When ${\mathcal M}$ is a matrix algebra in relations (9), it is called {\it finitely correlated state } and the general mathematical structures of such a translation invariant states on ${\mathcal B}$ were further investigated in details in [FNW2] [FNW3], [Ma1],[Ma2],[Ma3] and there afterward in [BJ] and [BJKW] for more general translation invariant states on ${\mathcal B}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Bernoulli state
nodes.statement: If ${\mathcal K}=\mathbb{C}$, then Popescu elements are just some complex numbers i.e. $v_k=\lambda_k$, then $\omega$ is a pure tensor product state. We call such a state a {\it Bernoulli state}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Isomorphism of translation dynamics
nodes.statement: Given two translation invariant states $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ on ${\mathcal B}$, when can we say their translation dynamics $({\mathcal B},\theta,\omega_1)$ and $({\mathcal B},\theta,\omega_2)$ are isomorphic? i.e. When can we say that there exists an automorphism $\alpha$ on ${\mathcal B}$ such that $\omega_2 \alpha =\omega_1$ and $\theta \alpha = \alpha \theta$ ?
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Weakly isomorphic translation dynamics
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let $\Theta_k:\pi_k({\mathcal B})'' \rightarrow \pi_k({\mathcal B})''$ be the associated automorphisms where $({\mathcal H},\pi_k,\Omega_k)$ are GNS spaces for $({\mathcal B},\omega_k) ,\;k=1,2$. $({\mathcal B},\theta,\omega_1)$ and $({\mathcal B},\theta,\omega_2)$ are said to be {\it weakly isomorphic} if there exists a unitary operator $U:{\mathcal H}_1 \rightarrow {\mathcal H}_2$ so that $U\Omega_1=\Omega_2$ and $U\Theta_1(X)U^*=\Theta_2(UXU^*)$ for all $X \in \pi_1({\mathcal B})''$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Ornstein's isomorphism theorem
nodes.statement: Kolmogorov-Sinai dynamical entropy [Pa] is an invariance for translation dynamics on classical spin chain on lattice $\mathbb{Z}$ and a celebrated result due to D. Ornstein [Or1] also says that Kolmogorov-Sinai dynamical entropy is a complete invariance for classical Markov states.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Projections e_n
nodes.statement: Given a translation invariant state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$, we set increasing sequence of projections $e_n=[\pi(\theta^n({\mathcal B}_R))'\Omega],\;n \in \mathbb{Z}$ in the GNS space $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ associated with state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Shift covariance of e_n
nodes.statement: It is simple to check that \begin{equation} S_me_nS_m^*=e_{n+m} \end{equation} where $S_m$ is the unitary operator implementing $\theta^m$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (17)
nodes.statement: S_me_nS_m^*=e_{n+m}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Kolmogorov property
nodes.statement: We say $\omega$ admits Kolmogorov property if $e_n \downarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ as $n \downarrow -\infty$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Kolmogorov property implies purity
nodes.statement: In particular Kolmogorov property implies purity of $\omega$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Type-I or type-III dichotomy for half-chain restrictions
nodes.statement: In [Mo4] we have shown that a translation invariant pure state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ can give only type-I or type-III factor states once we restrict to ${\mathcal B}_R$ (Theorem 3.4 in [Mo4] ).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
also_stated_at: In a recent paper [Mo3] it had been shown that for any translation invariant pure state $\omega$, $\omega_R$ is either a type-I or a type-III factor state.
Theorem 3.4 in [Mo4] says that $\omega_R$ is either a type-I or a type-III factor state on ${\mathcal B}_R$.

nodes.name: Restriction to B_R and isomorphism of pure translation dynamics
nodes.statement: One natural question that arises now for two such translation dynamics with pure states. How does restrictions of those states to ${\mathcal B}_R$ determine whether their dynamics are isomorphic or weakly isomorphic?
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Kolmogorov property and free energy density
nodes.statement: One related important question that also arises here how Kolmogorov property which is little stronger then purity can ensure existence of {\it free energy density } for a translation invariant state?
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual Popescu elements and their cp map
nodes.statement: Now consider the dual Popescu's elements $\tilde{{\mathcal P}}=({\mathcal K},\tilde{{\mathcal M}},\tilde{v}_k;1 \le k \le d,\;\Omega)$ and the completely positive map from $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ to ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ defined by $$\tilde{s}_I\tilde{s}_J^* \rightarrow \tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}^*_J,\;|I|,|J| < \infty$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Minimal Stinespring representation of the dual Cuntz algebra
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:\tilde{{\mathcal O}_d} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}})$ be the minimal Stinespring representation so that $P\pi(\tilde{s}_I\tilde{s}_J^*)P=\tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}_J^*$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty $.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual co-isometry relation (18)
nodes.statement: In particular we have \begin{equation} P\pi(\tilde{s}^*_i)P=\pi(\tilde{s}^*_i)P=\tilde{v}^*_i \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (18)
nodes.statement: P\pi(\tilde{s}^*_i)P=\pi(\tilde{s}^*_i)P=\tilde{v}^*_i
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual state psi-tilde
nodes.statement: We also consider the state $\tilde{\psi}$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ given by \begin{equation} \tilde{\psi}(\tilde{s}_I\tilde{s}_J^*)=\phi(\tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}^*_J) \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (19)
nodes.statement: \tilde{\psi}(\tilde{s}_I\tilde{s}_J^*)=\phi(\tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}^*_J)
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual state restricts to omega on B_L
nodes.statement: By relation (12) we check that $\tilde{\psi}|\mbox{UHF}_d=\omega|{\mathcal B}_L$ (see section 3).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Support projections e_0 and e-tilde_0
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We consider the GNS space $(H_0,\pi,\Omega)$ associated with $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$. Let $e_0=[\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'\Omega]$ and $\tilde{e}_0=[\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'\Omega]$ be the support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi({\mathcal B}_R)''$ and $\pi({\mathcal B}_L)''$ respectively.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Projection q_0 and subspace K_0
nodes.statement: We set projection $q_0=e_0 \tilde{e}_0$ and take ${\mathcal K}_0$ to be the subspace of ${\mathcal H}$ determined by the projection $q_0$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Corner algebras M^1_0 and M-tilde^1_0
nodes.statement: Also set von-Neumann algebras ${\mathcal M}^1_0=q_0\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''q_0$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1_0=q_0\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''q_0$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Corner algebras are factors
nodes.statement: Further $\omega$ being a factor state, we will also have factor property of ${\mathcal M}_0^1$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0^1$ ( Theorem 2.4 ).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Purity criterion and Haag duality for translation invariant factor states
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be a translation invariant factor state on ${\mathcal B}$ and $\psi$ be an extremal element in $K_{\omega}$. Then the following statements are equivalent: \vskip 1em 
oindent (a) $[{\mathcal M}^1_0\Omega]=I_{{\mathcal K}_0},\;[	ilde{{\mathcal M}}^1_0\Omega]=I_{{\mathcal K}_0}$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (b) $({\mathcal M}^1_0)'=	ilde{{\mathcal M}}^1_0$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (c) $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'=\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (d) $[\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'\Omega]=[\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''\Omega]$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (e) $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k 	ilde{v}_kx	ilde{v}_k^*= x \} ={\mathcal M}$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (f) $\omega$ is pure. \vskip 1em In such a case $	ilde{{\mathcal M}}^1_0 = \{x \in 	ilde{{\mathcal M}}:  eta_z(x)=x: z \in H \}$ where $H=\{ z \in S^1:\psi = \psi  eta_z \}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: For a translation invariant factor state, cyclicity of the corner algebras, Haag duality, the dual fixed-point condition and purity are all equivalent.
assumptions: $\omega$ be a translation invariant factor state on ${\mathcal B}$
conclusions:

nodes.name: Translation invariant pure states on B_R are product states
nodes.statement: One interesting result in [BJP] says that any translation invariant pure state on ${\mathcal B}_R$ is also a product state and the canonical endomorphism associated with two such states are unitary equivalent.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Mean entropy as invariant of translation dynamics
nodes.statement: In this context one interesting problem that remain open is whether mean entropy [Ru] is an invariance for translation dynamics.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Purity criterion via asymptotic sequences (Mohari)
nodes.statement: Theorem 3.2 in [Mo3] gives a precise answer: $\omega$ is pure if and only if there exists a sequence of positive contractive elements $x_n \in {\mathcal M}$ such that $$x_n \rightarrow I,\;\;x_{m+n}\tau_n(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)I$$ in strong operator topology for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$ and $m \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: $\omega$ is pure iff some positive contractions $x_n\to I$ asymptotically decouple $\tau_n(x)$ to $\phi(x)I$.

nodes.name: Gap in BJKW Theorem 7.1
nodes.statement: This statement can be taken as the correct version of Theorem 7.1 of [BJKW]. Theorem 7.1 in [BJKW] has aimed towards a sufficient condition on Popescu elements ${\mathcal P}$ for purity of the translation invariant state. However the statement and its proof are faulty as certain argument used in the proof is not time reversal symmetric and a factor state with Popescu elements on support projection satisfies the conditions of the statement of Theorem 7.1. One natural remedy to add additional hypothesis that (e) holds. In particular Lemma 7.6 in [BJKW] needs that additional assumption related to the support projection of the dual state $\tilde{\psi} \in K_{\tilde{\omega}}$. Besides this additional structure proof of Lemma 7.8 in [BJKW] is also not complete unless we find a proof for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$ ( we retained same notations here in the text) for such a factor state $\omega$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 7.1 of [BJKW] is faulty; it needs the extra hypothesis (e), and Lemmas 7.6 and 7.8 there are incomplete.

nodes.name: Normal conditional expectation
nodes.statement: For von-Neumann algebras ${\mathcal N} \subseteq {\mathcal M}$, a normal unital completely positive map $E_c:{\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal N}$ is called {\it normal conditional expectation } if \begin{equation} E_c(yxz)=yE_c(x)z \end{equation} for all $y,z \in {\mathcal N}$ and $x \in {\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Equation (20)
nodes.statement: E_c(yxz)=yE_c(x)z
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Takesaki's theorem on conditional expectations
nodes.statement: A theorem of Takesaki's [Ta, also see AcC] says that conditional expectation $E_c$ preserving a faithful normal state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ exists if and only if the modular group $\sigma=(\sigma_t:t \in \mathbb{R})$ associated with $\phi$, which preserves ${\mathcal M}$, also preserves ${\mathcal N}$, i.e. $\sigma_t(x) \in {\mathcal N}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in {\mathcal N}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: A $\phi$-preserving conditional expectation onto ${\mathcal N}$ exists iff the modular group of $\phi$ preserves ${\mathcal N}$.

nodes.name: Gap in the Keyl-Matsui-Schlingemann-Werner proof of Haag duality
nodes.statement: The paper ``On Haag Duality for Pure States of Quantum Spin Chain'' by authors: M. Keyl, Taku Matsui, D. Schlingemann, R. F. Werner, Rev. Math. Phys. 20:707-724,2008 has an incomplete proof for Haag duality property as Lemma 4.3 in that paper has a faulty argument.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: The earlier Haag duality proof of Keyl, Matsui, Schlingemann and Werner is incomplete (faulty Lemma 4.3).

nodes.name: Commutant lifting theorem (Popescu dilation)
nodes.statement:
Let $v_1,v_2,...,v_d$ be a family of bounded operators on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ so that $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$. Then there exists a unique up to isomorphism Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}$, a projection $P$ on ${\mathcal K}$ and a family of isometries $\{S_k:,\;1 \le k \le d \}$ satisfying Cuntz's relation so that  egin{equation} PS^{*}_{k}P=S_k^*P=v^*_k \end{equation} for all $1 \le k \le d$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation i.e. the vectors $\{ S_I{\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$. Moreover the following holds: 
oindent (a) $\Lambda^n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ where $\Lambda(X)=\sum_k S_kXS_k^*$; 
oindent (b) For any $D \in {\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K})=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): 	au(x)=\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kxv_k^*=x \}$, $\Lambda^n(D) ightarrow X'$ weakly as $n ightarrow \infty$ for some $X'$ in the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Moreover the self adjoint elements in the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$ is isometrically order isomorphic with the self adjoint elements in ${\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K})$ via the surjective map $X' ightarrow PX'P$, where ${\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K})=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_{1 \le k \le d } v_kxv^*_k=x \}.$ 
oindent (c) $\{v_k,v^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}' \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K})$ and equality holds if and only if $P \in \{S_k,S_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$. \vskip 1em If $(w_i)$ be another such an Popescu elements on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}'$ such that there exists an operator $u:{\mathcal K} ightarrow {\mathcal K}'$ so that $\sum_k w_kuv_k^*=u$ then there exists an operator $U:{\mathcal H}_v ightarrow {\mathcal H}_w$ so that $\pi'(x)U=U\pi(x)$ where $({\mathcal H}_w,\pi',S'_i)$ are Popescu dilation of $(w_i)$ and $\pi'$ is the associated minimal representation of ${\mathcal O}_d$. In particular $U$ is isometry, unitary if $u$ is so respectively. If $u$ is unitary and ${\mathcal K}={\mathcal K}'$ then we can as well take ${\mathcal H}_v={\mathcal H}_w$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Popescu elements dilate uniquely to Cuntz isometries; $\tau$-fixed points lift isometrically to the commutant of the dilation.
assumptions: $v_1,v_2,...,v_d$ be a family of bounded operators on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ so that $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$
conclusions: there exists a unique up to isomorphism Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}$, a projection $P$ on ${\mathcal K}$ and a family of isometries $\{S_k:,\;1 \le k \le d \}$ satisfying Cuntz's relation so that \begin{equation} PS^{*}_{k}P=S_k^*P=v^*_k \end{equation} for all $1 \le k \le d$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation i.e. the vectors $\{ S_I{\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$.

(b) For any $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kxv_k^*=x \}$, $\Lambda^n(D) \rightarrow X'$ weakly as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for some $X'$ in the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Moreover the self adjoint elements in the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$ is isometrically order isomorphic with the self adjoint elements in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ via the surjective map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$, where ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_{1 \le k \le d } v_kxv^*_k=x \}.$
(c) $\{v_k,v^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}' \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and equality holds if and only if $P \in \{S_k,S_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$.
also_stated_at: Given a Popescu's elements ${\mathcal P}=\{{\mathcal K},{\mathcal M}, v_i,\;1 \le i \le d, \sum_iv_iv^*_i=1 \}$, the map $$s_Is_J^* \rightarrow v_Iv_J^*$$ is unital completely positive from ${\mathcal O}_d$ to ${\mathcal M}$ and thus Stinespring minimal dilation gives a representation $\pi:{\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H})$, a Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}$ with a projection $P$ with range equal to ${\mathcal K}$ such that $$P\pi(s_i)^*P=\pi(s_i)^*P=v_i^*$$ and $\{\pi(s_I){\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ is total in ${\mathcal H}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Commutant lifting theorem (Popescu dilation)
nodes.statement: Following Popescu [Po] we define a completely positive map $R: {\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ by \begin{equation} R(s_Is^*_J)=v_Iv^*_J \end{equation} for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$. The representation $S_1,..,S_d$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$ on ${\mathcal H}$ thus may be taken to be the Stinespring dilation of $R$ [BR, vol-2] and uniqueness up to unitary equivalence follows from uniqueness of the Stinespring representation. That ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation follows from the minimality property of the Stinespring dilation. \vskip 1em For (a) let $Q$ be the limiting projection of $\Lambda^n(P)$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. Then we have $\Lambda(Q)=Q$ i.e. $Q\Lambda(I-Q)Q=0$ and so $(I-Q)S_k^*Q=0$. Interchanging the role of $Q$ with $I-Q$, we get $QS_k^*(I-Q)=0$. This shows $QS_k^*=S_k^*Q$ for all $1 le k \le d$. Since $Q$ is a projection, taking adjoint in the relation, we get $Q \in \{S_k,S^*_k\}'$. That $Q \ge P$ is obvious since $\Lambda^n(P) \ge P$ for all $n \ge 1$. In particular $QS_If=S_If$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and $|I| < \infty$. Hence $Q=I$ by the cyclicity of ${\mathcal K}$. \vskip 1em For (b) essentially we deffer from the argument used in Theorem 5.1 in [BJKW]. We fix any $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and note that $P\Lambda_k(D)P=\tau_k(D)=D$ for any $k \ge 1$. Thus for any integers $n > m$ we have $$\Lambda_m(P)\Lambda_n(D)\Lambda_m(P)=\Lambda_m(P\Lambda_{n-m}(D)P)=\Lambda_m(D)$$ Hence for any fixed $m \ge 1$ limit $<f,\Lambda_n(D)g>$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ exists for all $f,g \in \Lambda_m(P)$. Since the family of operators $\Lambda_n(D)$ is uniformly bounded and $\Lambda_m(P) \uparrow I$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$, a standard density argument guarantees that the weak operator limit of $\Lambda_n(D)$ exists as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Let $X'$ be the limit. So $\Lambda(X')=X'$, by Cuntz's relation, $X' \in \{S_k,S^*_k:1 \le k \le k \}'$. Since $P\Lambda_n(D)P=D$ for all $n \ge 1$, we also conclude that $PX'P=D$ by taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$. Conversely, it is obvious that $P\{ S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Hence we can identify $P\{S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P$ with ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. \vskip 1em Further it is obvious that $X'$ is self-adjoint if and only if $D=PX'P$ is self-adjoint ( since $\Lambda^n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, by taking limit $\Lambda^n(PXP)=\Lambda^n(PX^*P)$ shows that $X^*=X$ if $D^*=D$ ). Now fix any self-adjoint element $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Since the identity operator on ${\mathcal K}$ is an element in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ for any $\alpha \ge 0$ for which $- \alpha P \le D \le \alpha P$, we have $\alpha \Lambda_n(P) \le \Lambda_n(D) \le \alpha \Lambda_n(P)$ for all $n \ge 1$. By taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$ we conclude that $- \alpha I \le X' \le \alpha I$, where $PX'P=D$. Since operator norm of a self-adjoint element $A$ in a Hilbert space is given by $$||A||= \mbox{inf}_{\alpha \ge 0}\{\alpha: - \alpha I \le A \le \alpha I \}$$ we conclude that $||X'|| \le ||D||$. That $||D||=||PX'P|| \le ||X'||$ is obvious, $P$ being a projection. Thus the map is isometrically order isomorphic taking self-adjoint elements of the commutant to self-adjoint elements of ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. \vskip 1em We are left to prove (c). Inclusion is trivial. For the last part, we assume first that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For any element $D$ in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\{S_k,S^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d\}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Since $P$ commutes with $X'$, we verify that $$Dv^*_k= PX'PS^*_kP=PX'S^*_kP=PS^*_kX'P=PS^*_kPX'P=v^*_kD$$ We also have $D^* \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and thus $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Hence $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$. Since $P\pi_{\hat{\omega}} ({\mathcal O}_d)'P = {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. Thus equality holds whenever $P \in \{S_k,S_k^*,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$. \vskip 1em For the converse note that by commutant lifting property self-adjoint elements of the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}'$ is order isometric with the algebra ${\mathcal M}'$ via the map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$. Hence $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW]. \vskip 1em For the proof of intertwining relation and their property we refer to main body of the proof of Theorem 5.1 in [BJKW].

Thus for any integers $n > m$ we have $$\Lambda_m(P)\Lambda_n(D)\Lambda_m(P)=\Lambda_m(P\Lambda_{n-m}(D)P)=\Lambda_m(D)$$ Hence for any fixed $m \ge 1$ limit $<f,\Lambda_n(D)g>$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ exists for all $f,g \in \Lambda_m(P)$. Since $P\Lambda_n(D)P=D$ for all $n \ge 1$, we also conclude that $PX'P=D$ by taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$. Conversely, it is obvious that $P\{ S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Hence we can identify $P\{S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P$ with ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.

nodes.statement_short: Part (b): weak limit of $\Lambda_n(D)$ gives a commutant element compressing to $D$

nodes.name: Norm and order comparison shows the lifting is isometric
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Further it is obvious that $X'$ is self-adjoint if and only if $D=PX'P$ is self-adjoint ( since $\Lambda^n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, by taking limit $\Lambda^n(PXP)=\Lambda^n(PX^*P)$ shows that $X^*=X$ if $D^*=D$ ). Now fix any self-adjoint element $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Since the identity operator on ${\mathcal K}$ is an element in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ for any $\alpha \ge 0$ for which $- \alpha P \le D \le \alpha P$, we have $\alpha \Lambda_n(P) \le \Lambda_n(D) \le \alpha \Lambda_n(P)$ for all $n \ge 1$. By taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$ we conclude that $- \alpha I \le X' \le \alpha I$, where $PX'P=D$. Since operator norm of a self-adjoint element $A$ in a Hilbert space is given by $$||A||= \mbox{inf}_{\alpha \ge 0}\{\alpha: - \alpha I \le A \le \alpha I \}$$ we conclude that $||X'|| \le ||D||$. That $||D||=||PX'P|| \le ||X'||$ is obvious, $P$ being a projection. Thus the map is isometrically order isomorphic taking self-adjoint elements of the commutant to self-adjoint elements of ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.

nodes.statement_short: Norm and order comparison shows the lifting is isometric

nodes.name: Part (c): if $P$ is in the algebra, fixed points commute with the $v_k$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We are left to prove (c). Inclusion is trivial. For the last part, we assume first that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For any element $D$ in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\{S_k,S^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d\}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Since $P$ commutes with $X'$, we verify that $$Dv^*_k= PX'PS^*_kP=PX'S^*_kP=PS^*_kX'P=PS^*_kPX'P=v^*_kD$$ We also have $D^* \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and thus $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Hence $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$. Since $P\pi_{\hat{\omega}} ({\mathcal O}_d)'P = {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. Thus equality holds whenever $P \in \{S_k,S_k^*,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$.

Hence $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW].

nodes.name: Popescu's dilation
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em A family $(v_k,1 \le k \le d)$ of contractive operators on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ is called Popescu's elements if $\sum_kv_kv_k^*=I$ and the dilation $({\mathcal H},P,{\mathcal K},S_k,1 \le k \le d)$ in Theorem 2.1 is called Popescu's dilation to Cuntz elements.

nodes.name: States on O_d and Popescu systems correspondence
nodes.statement:
There exists a canonical one-one correspondence between the following objects: \vskip 1em 
oindent (a) States $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ \vskip 1em 
oindent (b) Function $C: {\mathcal I} 	imes {\mathcal I} ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with the following properties: 
oindent (i) $C(\emptyset, \emptyset)=1$; 
oindent (ii) for any function $\lambda:{\mathcal I} ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with finite support we have $$\sum_{I,J \in {\mathcal I}} \overline{\lambda(I)}C(I,J)\lambda(J) \ge 0$$ 
oindent (iii) $\sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_d} C(Ii,Ji) = C(I,J)$ for all $I,J \in {\mathcal I}$. \vskip 1em 
oindent (c) Unitary equivalence class of objects $({\mathcal K},\Omega,v_1,..,v_d)$ where 
oindent (i) ${\mathcal K}$ is a Hilbert space and $\Omega$ is a unit vector in ${\mathcal K}$; 
oindent (ii) $v_1,..,v_d \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ so that $\sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_d} v_iv^*_i=1$; 
oindent (iii) the linear span of the vectors of the form $v^*_I\Omega$, where $I \in {\mathcal I}$, is dense in ${\mathcal K}$. \vskip 1em The correspondence is given by a unique completely positive map $R: {\mathcal O}_d ightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$, where 
oindent (i) $R(s_Is^*_J)=v_Iv^*_J;$ 
oindent (ii) $\psi(x)=<\Omega,R(x)\Omega>;$ 
oindent (iii) $\psi(s_Is^*_J)=C(I,J)=<v^*_I \Omega,v^*_J\Omega>;$ 
oindent (iv) For any fixed $g \in U_d$, the completely positive map $R_g:{\mathcal O}_d ightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ defined by $R_g= R \circ  eta_g$ give rises to a Popescu system given by $({\mathcal K},\Omega, eta_g(v_i),.., eta_g(v_d))$ where $ eta_g(v_i)=\sum_{1 \le j \le d} \overline{g^i_j} v_j.$

nodes.name: Proof of Minimal Popescu elements of a state on O_d
nodes.statement: We fix a state $\psi$ and consider the GNS space $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ associated with $({\mathcal O}_d,\psi)$ and set $S_i=\pi(s_i)$. It is obvious that $S^*_kP \subseteq P$ for all $1 \le k \le d $, thus $P$ is the minimal subspace containing $\Omega$ and invariant by all $\{ S^*_k;\;1 \le k \le d \}$ i.e. \begin{equation} PS^*_kP=S^*_kP \end{equation} Thus $v^*_k=PS^*_kP=S_k^*P$ and so $\sum_k v_kv^*_k = \sum_k PS_kS^*_kP= P$ which is identity operator in ${\mathcal K}$. This completes the proof of (a) (b) and (c). \vskip 1em For (d) we note that $$\psi(s_Is^*_J)$$ $$=<\Omega, S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$ $$=<\Omega,PS_IS^*_JP\Omega>$$ $$=<\Omega,v_Iv^*_J\Omega>.$$ Since ${\mathcal H}$ is spanned by the vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega:|I|,|J| < \infty \}$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is spanned by the vectors $\{ S^*_J\Omega=v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$, ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for $S_I$ i.e. the vectors $\{ S_I{\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ spans ${\mathcal H}$. Uniqueness up to isomorphism follows as usual by total property of vectors $v^*_I\Omega$ in ${\mathcal K}$. \vskip 1em Conversely for a Popescu's elements $({\mathcal K},v_i,\Omega)$ satisfying (a) and (b), we consider the family $({\mathcal H},S_k,\;1 \le k \le d,P)$ of Cuntz's elements defined as in Theorem 2.1. We claim that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation $\pi(s_i) \rightarrow S_i$. Note that by our construction vectors $\{S_If,f \in {\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$ and $v^*_J\Omega=S^*_J\Omega$ for all $|J| < \infty$. Thus by our hypothesis that vectors $\{v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal K}$, we verify that vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$. Hence $\Omega$ is a cyclic for the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$. \vskip 1em We are left to prove (e) and (f). It simple to note by (d) that $\psi \lambda=\psi$ i.e. $$\sum_i <\Omega,S_iS_IS^*_JS^*_i\Omega>= \sum_i <\Omega,v_iv_Iv^*_Jv^*_i\Omega> $$ $$=<\Omega,v_Iv_J^*\Omega> = <\Omega,S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ where in the second equality we have used our hypothesis that the vector state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ is $\tau$-invariant. In such case we aim now to show that $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. To that end let $p'$ be the support projection in ${\mathcal M}$ for $\tau$ invariant state $\phi$. Thus $\phi(1-p') = 0$ i.e. $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and by invariance we also have $\phi(p'\tau(1-p')p')=\phi(1-p')=0$. Since $p'\tau(1-p')p' \ge 0 $ and an element in ${\mathcal M}$, by minimality of support projection, we conclude that $p'\tau(1-p')p'=0$. Hence $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and $p'v^*_kp'=v^*_kp'$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. Thus $p'v^*_I\Omega=v^*_I\Omega$ for all $|I| < \infty$. As ${\mathcal K}$ is the closed linear span of the vectors $\{ v_I^*\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$, we conclude that $p'=p$. In other words $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. This completes the proof for (e). \vskip 1em We are left to show (f) where we assume that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. $\Omega$ being a cyclic vector for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, the weak$^*$ limit of the increasing projection $\Lambda^k(P)$ is $I$. Thus by Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] we have $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic if and only if the reduced dynamics $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic. For the last part of the statement, we need to show for a projection $e \in {\mathcal M}$, $\tau(e)=e$ if and only if $e \in {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$. It is an easy consequence since $\tau(e)=e$ says that $e\tau(I-e)e=0$ and so $(1-e)v_k^*e=0$. Changing the role of $e$ by $I-e$, we also get $ev_k^*(I-e)=0$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. Thus we get that $e$ commutes with each $v_k$. $P$ being in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $v_k \in {\mathcal M}$. So $e \in {\mathcal M}'$. Thus by a standard theorem [La,Ev,Fr,BJKW] ergodic property is equivalent to factor property of ${\mathcal M}$.

nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We are left to prove (e) and (f). It simple to note by (d) that $\psi \lambda=\psi$ i.e. $$\sum_i <\Omega,S_iS_IS^*_JS^*_i\Omega>= \sum_i <\Omega,v_iv_Iv^*_Jv^*_i\Omega> $$ $$=<\Omega,v_Iv_J^*\Omega> = <\Omega,S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ where in the second equality we have used our hypothesis that the vector state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ is $\tau$-invariant. In such case we aim now to show that $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. To that end let $p'$ be the support projection in ${\mathcal M}$ for $\tau$ invariant state $\phi$. Thus $\phi(1-p') = 0$ i.e. $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and by invariance we also have $\phi(p'\tau(1-p')p')=\phi(1-p')=0$. Since $p'\tau(1-p')p' \ge 0 $ and an element in ${\mathcal M}$, by minimality of support projection, we conclude that $p'\tau(1-p')p'=0$. Hence $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and $p'v^*_kp'=v^*_kp'$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. Thus $p'v^*_I\Omega=v^*_I\Omega$ for all $|I| < \infty$. As ${\mathcal K}$ is the closed linear span of the vectors $\{ v_I^*\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$, we conclude that $p'=p$. In other words $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. This completes the proof for (e).

nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We are left to show (f) where we assume that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. $\Omega$ being a cyclic vector for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, the weak$^*$ limit of the increasing projection $\Lambda^k(P)$ is $I$. Thus by Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] we have $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic if and only if the reduced dynamics $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic. For the last part of the statement, we need to show for a projection $e \in {\mathcal M}$, $\tau(e)=e$ if and only if $e \in {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$. It is an easy consequence since $\tau(e)=e$ says that $e\tau(I-e)e=0$ and so $(1-e)v_k^*e=0$. Changing the role of $e$ by $I-e$, we also get $ev_k^*(I-e)=0$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. Thus we get that $e$ commutes with each $v_k$. $P$ being in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $v_k \in {\mathcal M}$. So $e \in {\mathcal M}'$. Thus by a standard theorem [La,Ev,Fr,BJKW] ergodic property is equivalent to factor property of ${\mathcal M}$.

nodes.name: Unique KMS state on O_d: phi need not be tau-invariant
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Before we move to our next result, we comment here that in general for a $\lambda$ invariant state on ${\mathcal O}_d$, the normal state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}=\{v_k,v_k^*:1 \le k \le d \}''$ need not be invariant for $\tau$. To that end we consider ( [BR] vol-II page 110 ) the unique KMS state $\psi=\psi_{\beta}$ for the automorphism $\alpha_t(s_i)=e^{it}s_i$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$. $\psi$ is $\lambda$ invariant and $\psi_{|\mbox{UHF}_d}$ is the unique faithful trace. $\psi$ being a KMS state for an automorphism, the normal state induced by the cyclic vector on $\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ is also separating for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. As $\psi \beta_z = \psi$ for all $z \in S^1$ we have $<\Omega,\pi(s_I)\Omega>=<\Omega,\beta_z(s_I)\Omega> = z^{|I|}<\Omega,\pi(s_I)\Omega>$ for all $z \in S^1$ and so $<\Omega,\pi(s_I)\Omega>=0$ for all $|I| \ge 1$. In particular $<\Omega,v_I^*\Omega>=0$ where $(v_i)$ are defined as in Proposition 2.3 and thus $<v_i\Omega,v^*_I\Omega>=<\Omega,v^*_iv_I\Omega>=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Hence $v_i\Omega=0$. By Proposition 2.3 (e), $\Omega$ is separating for ${\mathcal M}$ and so we get $v_i=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$ and this contradicts that $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=1$. Thus we conclude by Proposition 2.3 (e) that $\phi$ is not $\tau$ invariant on ${\mathcal M}$. This example also indicates that the support projection of a $\lambda$ invariant state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ need not be equal to the minimal sub-harmonic projection $P$ i.e. the closed span of vectors $\{ S_I^*\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$ containing $\Omega$ and $\{v_Iv_J^*: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ need not be even an algebra.

nodes.name: Popescu elements on the support projection of a lambda-invariant state
nodes.statement:
Let $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ be the GNS representation of a $\lambda$ invariant state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and $P$ be the support projection of the normal state $\psi_{\Omega}(X)=<\Omega,X\Omega>$ in the von-Neumann algebra $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. Then the following holds: \vskip 1em 
oindent (a) $P$ is a sub-harmonic projection for the endomorphism $\Lambda(X)=\sum_k S_kXS^*_k$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ i.e. $\Lambda(P) \ge P$ satisfying the following: \vskip 1em 
oindent (i) $\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (ii) $PS^*_kP=S^*_kP,\;\;1 \le k \le d$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (iii) $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$ where $S_k=\pi(s_k)$ and $v_k=PS_kP$ for $1 \le k \le d$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (b) For any $I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_k),J=(j_1,j_2,...,j_l)$ with $|I|,|J| < \infty$ we have $\psi(s_Is^*_J) = <\Omega,v_Iv^*_J\Omega>$ and the vectors $\{ S_If: f \in {\mathcal K},\;|I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (c) The von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}=P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P$, acting on the Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ i.e. the range of $P$, is generated by $\{v_k,v^*_k:1 \le k \le d \}''$ and the normal state $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x \Omega>$ is faithful on the von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}$. \vskip 1em 
oindent (d) The self-adjoint part of the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ is norm and order isomorphic to the space of self-adjoint fixed points of the completely positive map $	au$. The isomorphism takes $X' \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ onto $PX'P \in {\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K})$, where ${\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K}) = \{ x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): 	au(x)=x \}$ and $	au(x)=\sum_kv_kxv^*_k,\;x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. Furthermore ${\mathcal M}' = {\mathcal B}_{	au}({\mathcal K})$. \vskip 1em Conversely let ${\mathcal M}$ be a von-Neumann algebra generated by a family $\{v_k: 1 \le k \le d \}$ of bounded operators on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ so that $\sum_kv_kv_k^*=1$ and the commutant  egin{equation} {\mathcal M}'=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k v_kxv_k^*=x \} \end{equation} Then the Popescu dilation $({\mathcal H},P,S_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ described in Theorem 2.1 satisfies the following: \vskip 1em 
oindent (i) $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (ii) For any faithful normal $	au-$invariant state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ there exists a state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ defined by $$\psi(s_Is^*_J)=\phi(v_Iv^*_J),\;|I|,|J| < \infty $$ such that the GNS space associated with $({\mathcal M},\phi)$ is the support projection for $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ satisfying (a)-(d). \vskip 1em Further for a given $\lambda$-invariant state $\psi$, the family $({\mathcal K},{\mathcal M},v_k\;1 \le k \le d,\phi)$ satisfying (a)-(d) is determined uniquely up to unitary conjugation. \vskip 1em 
oindent (e) $\phi$ is a faithful normal $	au$-invariant state on ${\mathcal M}$. Furthermore the following statements are equivalent: 
oindent (i) $({\mathcal O}_d,\lambda,\psi)$ is ergodic; 
oindent (ii) $({\mathcal M},	au,\phi)$ is ergodic; 
oindent (iii) ${\mathcal M}$ is a factor.

nodes.name: Proof of Popescu elements on the support projection of a lambda-invariant state
nodes.statement: $\Lambda(P)$ is also a projection in $\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ so that $\psi_{\Omega}(\Lambda(P))=1$ by invariance property. Thus we have $\Lambda(P) \ge P$ i.e. $P\Lambda(I-P)P=0$. Hence we have \begin{equation} PS^*_kP=S^*_kP \end{equation} Moreover by $\lambda$ invariance property we also note that the faithful normal state $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x\Omega>$ on the von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}=P\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''P$ is invariant for the reduced Markov map [Mo1] on ${\mathcal M}$ given by \begin{equation} \tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P \end{equation} \vskip 1em We claim that $\mbox{lim}_{n \uparrow \infty}\Lambda^n(P)= I$. That $\{ \Lambda^n(P): n \ge 1 \}$ is a sequence of increasing projections follows from sub-harmonic property of $P$ and endomorphism property of $\Lambda$. Let the limiting projection be $Y$. Then $\Lambda(Y)=Y$ and so $Y \in \{S_k,S^*_k \}'$. Since by our construction, the GNS Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\hat{\omega}}}$ is generated by $S_IS^*_J\Omega$, $Y$ is a scalar. $Y$ being a non-zero projection, it is the identity operator in ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\psi}}$. \vskip 1em Now it is routine to verify (a) (b) and (c). For the first part of (d) we appeal to Theorem 2.1. For the last part note that for any invariant element $D$ in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Since $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ we note that $(1-P)X'P=0$. Now since $X' \in \{ S_k,S^*_k \}'$, we verify that $Dv^*_k= PXPS^*_kP=PXS^*_kP=PS^*_kXP=PS^*_kPXP=v^*_kD$. Since $D^* \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ we also have $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Thus $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'={\mathcal M}'$. Since $P\pi_{\hat{\omega}}({\mathcal O}_d)'P= {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. The reverse inclusion is trivial. This completes the proof for (d). \vskip 1em For the converse part: for (i), since by our assumption and the commutant lifting property self-adjoint elements of the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}'$ is order isometric with the algebra ${\mathcal M}'$ via the map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$, $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW]. For (ii) without loss of generality, we assume that $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x\Omega>$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$ and $\Omega$ is a cyclic and separating vector for ${\mathcal M}$. ( otherwise we set state $\psi(s_Is^*_J)=\phi(v_Iv_J^*)$ and consider its GNS representation ) We are left to show that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation $\pi(s_i) \rightarrow S_i$. To that end let $Y \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ be the projection on the subspace generated by the vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$. Note that, $P$ being an element in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $Y$ also commutes with all the elements of $P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P=P {\mathcal M} P$. Hence $Yx\Omega=x\Omega$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$. Thus $Y \ge P$. Since $\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ by our construction, we conclude that $Y=\Lambda_n(Y) \ge \Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. Hence $Y=I$. In other words $\Omega$ is cyclic for the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$. This completes the proof for (ii). \vskip 1em Uniqueness up to unitary isomorphism follows as GNS representation is determined uniquely up to unitary conjugation and so its support projection. \vskip 1em The first part of (e) we note that $PS_IS^*_JP=v_Iv_J^*$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ and thus ${\mathcal M}=P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P$ is the von-Neumann algebra generated by $\{v_k,v_k^*:1 \le k \le d \}$ and thus $\tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$. That $\phi$ is $\tau(x)=\sum_k v_kxv_k^*$ invariant follows as $\psi$ is $\lambda$-invariant. We are left to prove equivalence of statements (i)-(iii). \vskip 1em By Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] the Markov semi-group $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic if and only if $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic ( here we need to recall by (a) that $\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ ). By a standard result [Ev, also BJKW] $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic if and only if there is no non trivial projection $e$ invariant for $\tau$ i.e. ${\mathcal I}^{\tau} = \{e \in {\mathcal M}: e^*=e,e^2=e,\tau(e)=e \}=\{0,1 \}$. If $\tau(e)=e$ for some projection $e \in {\mathcal M} $ then $(1-e)\tau(e)(1-e)=0$ and so $ev^*_k(1-e)=0$. Same is true if we replace $e$ by $1-e$ as $\tau(1-e)=\tau(1)-\tau(e)=1-e$ and so $(1-e)v^*_ke=0$. Thus $e$ commutes with $v_k,v_k^*$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. Hence ${\mathcal I}^{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$. Inequality in the reverse direction is trivial and thus ${\mathcal I}^{\tau}$ is trivial if and only if ${\mathcal M}$ is a factor. This shows equivalence of (ii) and (iii) follows by a standard result [La,Fr] in non-commutative ergodic theory. This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Gauge stabilizer subgroup of a lambda-invariant factor state
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi$ be a $\lambda$ invariant factor state on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ be its GNS representation. Then the following holds: 
oindent (a) The closed subgroup $H=\{z \in S^1: \psi  eta_z =\psi \}$ is equal to $$\{z \in S^1:  eta_z \mbox{extends to an automorphism of } \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \} $$ 
oindent (b) Let ${\mathcal O}_d^{H}$ be the fixed point sub-algebra in ${\mathcal O}_d$ under the action of gauge group $\{  eta_z: z \in H \}$. Then $\pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})'' = \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''$. 
oindent (c) If $H$ is a finite cyclic group of $k$ many elements and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a factor, then $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''  igcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)' \equiv \mathbb{C}^m$ where $1 \le m \le k$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The gauge stabilizer $H$ of $\psi$ equals the set of extendable gauge automorphisms, and $H$-fixed points generate $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''$.
assumptions: $\psi$ be a $\lambda$ invariant factor state on ${\mathcal O}_d$

nodes.name: Proof of Gauge stabilizer subgroup of a lambda-invariant factor state
nodes.statement: It is simple that $H$ is a closed subgroup. For any fix $z \in H $ we define unitary operator $U_z$ extending the map $\pi(x)\Omega \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))\Omega$ and check that the map $X \rightarrow U_zXU^*_z$ extends $\beta_z$ to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For the converse we will use the hypothesis that $\psi$ is a $\lambda$-invariant factor state and $\beta_z \lambda= \lambda \beta_z$ to guarantee that $\psi \beta_z (X) = {1 \over n} \sum_{1 \le k \le n} \psi \lambda^k \beta_z(X) = {1 \over n} \sum_{1 \le k \le n} \psi \beta_z \lambda^k(X) \rightarrow \psi(X)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for any $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, where we have used the same symbol $\beta_z$ for the extension. Hence $z \in H$. \vskip 1em In the following instead of working with ${\mathcal O}_d$ we should be working with the inductive limit $C^*$ algebra and their inductive limit states. For simplicity of notation we still use $UHF_d,{\mathcal O}_d$ for its inductive limit of ${\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow^{\lambda} {\mathcal O}_d$ and $UHF_d \rightarrow^{\lambda} UHF_d$ respectively and so for its inductive limit states. \vskip 1em Now we aim to prove (b). $H$ being a closed subgroup of $S^1$, it is either entire $S^1$ or a finite subgroup $\{exp({ 2i \pi l \over k})|l=0,1,...,k-1 \}$ where the integer $k \ge 1$. If $H=S^1$ we have nothing to prove for (b). When $H$ is a finite closed subgroup, we identify $[0,1)$ with $S^1$ by the usual map and note that if $\beta_t$ is restricted to $t \in [0,{1 \over k})$, then by scaling we check that $\beta_t$ defines a representation of $S^1$ in automorphisms of ${\mathcal O}^H_d$. Now we consider the direct integral representation $\pi'$ defined by $$\pi'= \int^{\oplus}_{[0,{1 \over k})} dt \pi_{|_{{\mathcal O}^H_d}} \beta_t $$ of ${\mathcal O}_d^{H}$ on ${\mathcal H}_{|_{{\mathcal O}_d^H}}\otimes L^2([0,{1 \over k})\;)$, where ${\mathcal H}_{|_{{\mathcal O}_d^H}}$ is the cyclic space of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d^H)$ generated by $\Omega$. That it is indeed direct integral follows as states $\psi \beta_{t_1}$ and $\psi \beta_{t_2}$ are either same or orthogonal for a factor state $\psi$ (see the proof of Lemma 7.4 in [BJKW] for further details). Interesting point here to note that the new representation $\pi'$ is $(\beta_t)$ co-variant i.e. $\pi' \beta_t=\beta_t \pi' $, hence by simplicity of the $C^*$ algebra ${\mathcal O}_d$ we conclude that $$\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi'({\mathcal O}_d^{H})''^{\beta_t}$$ \vskip 1em By exploring the hypothesis that $\psi$ is a factor state, we also have as in Lemma 6.11 in [BJKW] $I \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;) \subset \pi'({\mathcal O}_d^H)''$. Hence we also have $$\pi'({\mathcal O}_d^H)''= \pi({\mathcal O}_d^H)'' \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;).$$ Since $\beta_t$ is acting as translation on $I \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;)$ which being an ergodic action, we have $$\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})'' \otimes 1$$ Since $\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' \otimes 1$, we conclude that $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})''$. \vskip 1em A proof for the statement (c) follows from Lemma 7.12 in [BJKW]. The original idea of the proof can be traced back to Arveson's work on spectrum of an automorphism of a commutative compact group [Ar1].
