nodes.name: Standing Popescu system with invariant faithful state
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em To that end let ${\mathcal M}$ be a von-Neumann algebra acting on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ and $\{v_k,\;1 \le k \le d\}$ be a family of bounded operators on ${\mathcal K}$ so that ${\mathcal M}=\{v_k,v_k^*,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$ and $\sum_kv_kv^*_k=1$. Furthermore let $\Omega$ be a cyclic and separating vector for ${\mathcal M}$ so that the normal state $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x\Omega>$ on ${\mathcal M}$ is invariant for the Markov map $\tau$ on ${\mathcal M}$ defined by $\tau(x)=\sum_kv_kxv^*_k$ for $x \in {\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Translation invariant state from a Popescu system
nodes.statement: Let $\omega$ be the translation invariant state on UHF$_d =\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}M_d$ defined by $$\omega(e^{i_1}_{j_1}(l) \otimes e^{i_2}_{j_2}(l+1) \otimes ....\otimes e^{i_n}_{j_n}(l+n-1)) = \phi(v_Iv^*_J)$$ where $e^i_j(l)$ is the elementary matrix at lattice site $l \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Dual Popescu elements v-tilde_k
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We set $\tilde{v}_k = \overline{ {\mathcal J} \sigma_{i \over 2}(v^*_k) {\mathcal J} } \in {\mathcal M}'$ ( see [BJKW] for details ) where ${\mathcal J}$ and $\sigma=(\sigma_t,\;t \in \mathbb{R})$ are Tomita's conjugation operator and modular automorphisms associated with $\phi$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Dual Popescu elements relations
nodes.statement: By KMS or modular relation [BR vol-1] we verify that $$\sum_k \tilde{v}_k \tilde{v}_k^*=1$$ and \begin{equation} \phi(v_Iv^*_J)= \phi(\tilde{v}_{\tilde{I}}\tilde{v}^*_{\tilde{J}}) \end{equation} where $\tilde{I}=(i_n,..,i_2,i_1)$ if $I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_n)$. Moreover $\tilde{v}^*_I\Omega = {\mathcal J} \sigma_{i \over 2}(v_{\tilde{I}})^*{\mathcal J}\Omega= {\mathcal J} \Delta^{1 \over 2}v_{\tilde{I}}\Omega =v^*_{\tilde{I}}\Omega$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Equation (29)
nodes.statement: \phi(v_Iv^*_J)= \phi(\tilde{v}_{\tilde{I}}\tilde{v}^*_{\tilde{J}})
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Popescu dilations of v and v-tilde
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let $({\mathcal H},P,S_k,\;1 \le k \le d )$ and $(\tilde{{\mathcal H}},P,\tilde{S}_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ be the Popescu dilation described as in Theorem 2.1 associated with $({\mathcal K},v_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ and ${\mathcal K},\tilde{v}_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ respectively.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Amalgamated tensor product
nodes.statement: Following [BJKW] we consider the amalgamated tensor product ${\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ of ${\mathcal H}$ with $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ over the joint subspace ${\mathcal K}$. It is the completion of the quotient of the set $$\mathbb{C} \bar{I} \otimes \mathbb{C} I \otimes {\mathcal K},$$ where $\bar{I},I$ both consist of all finite sequences with elements in $\{1,2, ..,d \}$, by the equivalence relation defined by a semi-inner product defined on the set by requiring $$<\bar{I} \otimes I \otimes f,\bar{I}\bar{J} \otimes IJ \otimes g>=<f,\tilde{v}_{\bar{J}}v_Jg>,$$ $$<\bar{I}\bar{J} \otimes I \otimes f, \bar{I} \otimes IJ \otimes g> =<\tilde{v}_{\bar{J}}f,v_Jg>$$ and all inner product that are not of these form are zero.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Hilbert space amalgamating the two dilations over ${\mathcal K}$ via an explicit semi-inner product on words.

nodes.name: Commuting representations on the amalgamated space
nodes.statement: We also define two commuting representations $(S_i)$ and $(\tilde{S}_i)$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$ on ${\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ by the following prescription: $$S_I\lambda(\bar{J} \otimes J \otimes f)=\lambda(\bar{J} \otimes IJ \otimes f),$$ $$\tilde{S}_{\bar{I}}\lambda(\bar{J} \otimes J \otimes f)=\lambda(\bar{J}\bar{I} \otimes J \otimes f),$$ where $\lambda$ is the quotient map from the index set to the Hilbert space.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Co-isometry relations on the amalgamated space
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be the projection onto ${\mathcal K}$. Then we have $$S_i^*P=PS_i^*P=v_i^*$$ $$\tilde{S}_i^*P=P\tilde{S}_i^*P=\tilde{v}^*_i$$ for all $1 \le i \le d$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Amalgamated representation of the dual pair of Cuntz algebras
nodes.statement:
The following holds: 
oindent (a) For any $1 \le i,j \le d$ and $|I|,|J|< \infty$ and $| ar{I}|,| ar{J}| < \infty$ $$<\Omega,	ilde{S}_{ ar{I}}	ilde{S}^*_{ ar{J}} S_iS_IS^*_JS^*_j \Omega>=<\Omega, 	ilde{S}_i 	ilde{S}_{ ar{I}}	ilde{S}^*_{ ar{J}}	ilde{S}^*_jS_IS^*_J \Omega>;$$ 
oindent (b) The vector state $\psi_{\Omega}$ on $$	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d \equiv \otimes_{-\infty}^0 M_d \otimes_1^{\infty}M_d \equiv \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} M_d$$ is equal to $\omega$; 
oindent (c) $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ if and only if $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): 	au(x)=x,\; 	ilde{	au}(x)=x \}= \{zI: z \in \mathbb{C} \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: On the amalgamated space the vector state is $\omega$, and the representation is irreducible iff the common fixed points of $\tau,\tilde\tau$ are scalars.

nodes.name: Proof of Amalgamated representation of the dual pair of Cuntz algebras
nodes.statement: By our construction $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega =\tilde{v}^*_i\Omega=v_i^*\Omega=S_i^*\Omega$. Now (a) and (b) follow by repeated application of $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and the commuting property of the two representation $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes I)$ and $\pi(I \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)$. The last statement (c) follows from a more general fact proved below that the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is order isomorphic with the set $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=x,\; \tilde{\tau}(x)=x \}= \{zI: z \in \mathbb{C} \}$ via the map $X \rightarrow PXP$ where $X$ is the weak$^*$ limit of $\{\Lambda^m\tilde{\Lambda}^n(x)$ as $(m,n) \rightarrow (\infty,\infty)$. For details let $Y$ be the strong limit of increasing sequence of projections $(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^n(P)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then $Y$ commutes with $S_i\tilde{S}_j, S^*_i\tilde{S}^*_j$ for all $1 \le i,j \le d$. As $\Lambda(P)) \ge P$, we also have $\Lambda(Y) \ge Y$. Hence $(1-Y)S_i^*Y=0$. As $Y$ commutes with $S_i\tilde{S}_j$ we get $(1-Y)S_i^*S_i\tilde{S}_jY=0$ i.e. $(1-Y)\tilde{S}_jY=0$ for all $1 \le j \le d$. By symmetry of the argument we also get $(1-Y)S_iY=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Hence $Y$ commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and by symmetry of the argument $Y$ commutes as well with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. As $Yf=f$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$ we conclude that $Y=I$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$. \vskip 1em Let $x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ so that $\tau(x)=x$ and $\tilde{\tau}(x) = x $ then as in the proof of Theorem 2.1 we also check that $(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P) \Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) (\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P)$ is independent of $m,n$ as long as $m,n \ge k$. Hence the weak$^*$ limit $\Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) \rightarrow X$ exists as $m,n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore the limiting element $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$ and $PXP=x$. That the map $X \rightarrow PXP$ is an order-isomorphic on the set of self adjoint elements follows as in Theorem 2.1. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Repeated use of $\tilde S^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and commutant lifting for the joint fixed points.

nodes.name: Parts (a),(b) from $\tilde S_i^*\Omega=S_i^*\Omega$ and commutation
nodes.statement: By our construction $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega =\tilde{v}^*_i\Omega=v_i^*\Omega=S_i^*\Omega$. Now (a) and (b) follow by repeated application of $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and the commuting property of the two representation $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes I)$ and $\pi(I \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Parts (a),(b) from $\tilde S_i^*\Omega=S_i^*\Omega$ and commutation

nodes.name: Reduce (c) to an order isomorphism for joint fixed points
nodes.statement: The last statement (c) follows from a more general fact proved below that the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is order isomorphic with the set $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=x,\; \tilde{\tau}(x)=x \}= \{zI: z \in \mathbb{C} \}$ via the map $X \rightarrow PXP$ where $X$ is the weak$^*$ limit of $\{\Lambda^m\tilde{\Lambda}^n(x)$ as $(m,n) \rightarrow (\infty,\infty)$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Reduce (c) to an order isomorphism for joint fixed points

nodes.name: Limit projection $Y$ commutes with both algebras, so $Y=I$
nodes.statement: For details let $Y$ be the strong limit of increasing sequence of projections $(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^n(P)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then $Y$ commutes with $S_i\tilde{S}_j, S^*_i\tilde{S}^*_j$ for all $1 \le i,j \le d$. As $\Lambda(P)) \ge P$, we also have $\Lambda(Y) \ge Y$. Hence $(1-Y)S_i^*Y=0$. As $Y$ commutes with $S_i\tilde{S}_j$ we get $(1-Y)S_i^*S_i\tilde{S}_jY=0$ i.e. $(1-Y)\tilde{S}_jY=0$ for all $1 \le j \le d$. By symmetry of the argument we also get $(1-Y)S_iY=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Hence $Y$ commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and by symmetry of the argument $Y$ commutes as well with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. As $Yf=f$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$ we conclude that $Y=I$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Limit projection $Y$ commutes with both algebras, so $Y=I$

nodes.name: Lift joint fixed points as in Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let $x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ so that $\tau(x)=x$ and $\tilde{\tau}(x) = x $ then as in the proof of Theorem 2.1 we also check that $(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P) \Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) (\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P)$ is independent of $m,n$ as long as $m,n \ge k$. Hence the weak$^*$ limit $\Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) \rightarrow X$ exists as $m,n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore the limiting element $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$ and $PXP=x$. That the map $X \rightarrow PXP$ is an order-isomorphic on the set of self adjoint elements follows as in Theorem 2.1. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Lift joint fixed points as in Theorem 2.1

nodes.name: Amalgamated space is the Popescu dilation of v_i v-tilde_j
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em In short Proposition 3.1 also says that $(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H},S_i\tilde{S}_j\;1 \le i,j \le d,P)$ is the Popescu dilation associated with Popescu elements $({\mathcal K},v_i\tilde{v_j},1 \le i,j \le d \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Unique KMS state: M-tilde equals M' but corner space not an algebra
nodes.statement: Going back to our starting example of unique KMS state for the automorphisms $\beta_t(s_i)= ts_i,\;t \in S^1$, we check that $v^*_k=S^*_k$, ${\mathcal J} \tilde{v}^*_k {\mathcal J} = {1 \over d} S_k$ and thus equality holds i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$. But the corner vector space $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_c=P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P$ generated by the elements $\{\tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}^*_J: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ fails to be an algebra.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Does M' equal M-tilde for extremal psi and factor omega
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em \noindent (a) Does the equality ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ hold in general for an extremal element $\psi \in K_{\omega'}$ and a factor state $\omega$?
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
also_stated_at: A major problem that we will have to address is: when equality holds and its relation to Haag duality property (16).

nodes.name: When is the dual corner space an algebra
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em \noindent (b) When can we expect $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_c$ to be a $*$-algebra and so equal to $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$?
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Irreducibility of the amalgamated representation and gauge groups
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be a translation invariant factor state on ${\mathcal B}$ and $\psi$ be an extremal point in $K_{\omega'}$. We consider the amalgamated representation $\pi$ of $	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ in $	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ where the Popescu's elements $({\mathcal K},{\mathcal M},v_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ are taken as in Proposition 2.4. Then the following statements hold: \vskip 1em 
oindent (a) $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$. Furthermore $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ are factors and the following sets are equal: 
oindent (i) $H=\{ z \in S^1: \psi  eta_z = \psi \}$; 
oindent (ii) $H_{\pi} = \{ z :  eta_z \mbox{ extends to an automorphisms of } \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \}$; 
oindent (iii) $	ilde{H}_{\pi}= \{ z :  eta_z \mbox{ extends to an automorphisms of } \pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'' \}$. Moreover $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes I)''$ and $\pi(I \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ are factors. \vskip 1em 
oindent (b) $z ightarrow U_z$ is the unitary representation of $H$ in the Hilbert space $	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ defined by $U_z(\pi(	ilde{s}_j \otimes s_i )\Omega=\pi(z	ilde{s}_j \otimes zs_i)\Omega$ \vskip 1em 
oindent (c) The commutant of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d )''$ is invariant by the canonical endomorphisms $\Lambda(X)=\sum_i S_iXS_i^*$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}(X) = \sum_i 	ilde{S}_iX 	ilde{S}^*_i$. Same is true for each $i$ that the surjective map $X ightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ keeps the commutant of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ invariant. Same holds for the map $X ightarrow 	ilde{S}^*_iX	ilde{S}_i$. \vskip 1em 
oindent (d) The centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d )''$ is invariant by the canonical endomorphisms $\Lambda(X)=\sum_i S_iXS_i^*$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}(X) = \sum_i 	ilde{S}_iX 	ilde{S}^*_i$. Moreover for each $i$, the surjective map $X ightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ keeps the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ invariant. Same holds for the map $X ightarrow 	ilde{S}^*_iX	ilde{S}_i$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: For an extremal $\psi$, the amalgamated representation is irreducible, both Cuntz factors are factors with the same gauge stabilizer $H$, and Cuntz maps preserve the UHF commutant/centre.

nodes.name: Proof of Irreducibility of the amalgamated representation and gauge groups
nodes.statement: $P$ being the support projection by Proposition 2.4 we have $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k v_k x v_k^*= x\} = {\mathcal M}'$. That $({\mathcal M}',\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is ergodic follows from a general result [Mo1] ( see also [BJKW] for a different proof ) as $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic for a factor state $\psi$ being an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (Proposition 2.6). Hence $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=\tilde{\tau}(x)=x \} = \mathbb{C}$. Hence by Proposition 3.1, we conclude that $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$. That both $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ are factors follows trivially as $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''={\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$. \vskip 1em By the discussion above we first recall that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation of $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$. Let $G = \{ z=(z_1,z_2) \in S^1 \times S^1: \beta_z \mbox{ extends to an automorphism }$ $\mbox{on}\; \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'' \}$ be the closed subgroup where $$\beta_{(z_1,z_2)}(\tilde{s}_j \otimes s_i)=z_1 \tilde{s}_j \otimes z_2s_i .$$ By repeated application of the fact that $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and $S_i^*\Omega=\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega$ as in Proposition 3.1 (a) we verify that $\psi \beta_{(z,z)}=\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ if $z \in H$. For $z \in H $ we set unitary operator $U_z \pi(x \otimes y) \Omega = \pi(\beta_z(x) \otimes \beta_z(y))\Omega$ for all $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ and $y \in {\mathcal O}_d$. Thus we have $U_z\pi(s_i)U_z^*=z\pi(s_i)$ and also $U_z\pi(\tilde{s}_i)U_z^*=z\tilde{s}_i.$ By taking its restriction to $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ respectively we check that $H \subseteq \tilde{H}_{\pi} $ and $H \subseteq H_{\pi}$. \vskip 1em For the converse let $z \in H_{\pi}$ and we use the same symbol $\beta_z$ for the extension to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. By taking the inverse map we check easily that $\bar{z} \in H_{\pi}$ and in fact $H_{\pi}$ is a subgroup of $S^1$. Since $\lambda$ commutes with $\beta_z$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$, the canonical endomorphism $\Lambda$ defined by $\Lambda(X) = \sum_k S_kXS_k^*$ also commutes with the extension of $\beta_z$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. Note that the map $\pi(x)_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} $ for $x \in {\mathcal O}_d$ is a well defined $*$-homomorphism. Since same is true for $\bar{z}$ and $\beta_z\beta_{\bar{z}}=I$, the map is an isomorphism. Hence $\beta_z$ extends uniquely to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ commuting with the restriction of the canonical endomorphism on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{|{\mathcal H}}$. Since $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ is a factor, we conclude as in Proposition 2.5 (a) that $z \in H$. Thus $H_{\pi} \subseteq H$. As $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is also a factor, we also have $\tilde{H}_{\pi} \subseteq H$. Hence we have $H=H_{\pi}=\tilde{H}_{\pi}$ and $\{(z,z): z \in H \} \subseteq G \subseteq H \times H$. \vskip 1em For the second part of (a) we will adopt the argument used for Proposition 2.5. To that end we first note that $\Omega$ being a cyclic vector for the representation $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ in the Hilbert space $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $, by Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] (note that the proof only needs the cyclic property ) the representation of UHF$_d$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $ is quasi-equivalent to its sub-representation on the cyclic space generated by $\Omega$. On the other hand, by our hypothesis that $\omega$ is a factor state, Power's theorem [Pow] ensures that the state $\omega'$ (i.e. the restriction of $\omega$ to ${\mathcal B}_R$ which is identified here with $\mbox{UHF}_d$ ) is also a factor state on $\mbox{UHF}_d$. Hence quasi-equivalence ensures that $\pi(I \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a factor. We also note that the argument used in Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] is symmetric i.e. same argument is also valid for $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$. Thus $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes I)''$ is also a factor. This completes the proof of (a). We have proved (b) while giving proof of (a). \vskip 1em For $X \in {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$, as $\Lambda(X)$ commutes with $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ and $\{ S_iS^*_j: 1 \le i,j \le d \}$ we verify by Cuntz's relation that $\Lambda(X)$ is also an element in the commutant of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ once $X$ is so. It is also obvious that $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ if $X$ is so. Thus $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. For the last statement consider the map $X \rightarrow S_i^*XS_i$ on $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ which is clearly onto by Cuntz relation (3). Hence we need to show that $S^*_iXS_i$ is an element in the commutant whenever $X$ is so. To that end note that $S_i^*XS_i S_i^*YS_i=S_i^*S_iS_i^*XYS_i=S_i^*YXS_i=S^*_iYS_iS_i^*XS_i$ since $X$ commutes with $S_iS_i^*$. Thus onto property of the map ensures that $S_i^*XS_i$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. This completes the proof of (c) and (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Ergodicity of $(\mathcal M,\tau,\phi)$ plus Proposition 3.1 gives irreducibility; gauge extension arguments.

nodes.name: Ergodicity and Proposition 3.1 give irreducibility and factoriality
nodes.statement: $P$ being the support projection by Proposition 2.4 we have $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k v_k x v_k^*= x\} = {\mathcal M}'$. That $({\mathcal M}',\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is ergodic follows from a general result [Mo1] ( see also [BJKW] for a different proof ) as $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic for a factor state $\psi$ being an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (Proposition 2.6). Hence $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=\tilde{\tau}(x)=x \} = \mathbb{C}$. Hence by Proposition 3.1, we conclude that $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$. That both $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ are factors follows trivially as $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''={\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Ergodicity and Proposition 3.1 give irreducibility and factoriality

nodes.name: Gauge unitaries $U_z$ show $H\subseteq H_\pi,\tilde H_\pi$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em By the discussion above we first recall that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation of $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$. Let $G = \{ z=(z_1,z_2) \in S^1 \times S^1: \beta_z \mbox{ extends to an automorphism }$ $\mbox{on}\; \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'' \}$ be the closed subgroup where $$\beta_{(z_1,z_2)}(\tilde{s}_j \otimes s_i)=z_1 \tilde{s}_j \otimes z_2s_i .$$ By repeated application of the fact that $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and $S_i^*\Omega=\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega$ as in Proposition 3.1 (a) we verify that $\psi \beta_{(z,z)}=\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ if $z \in H$. For $z \in H $ we set unitary operator $U_z \pi(x \otimes y) \Omega = \pi(\beta_z(x) \otimes \beta_z(y))\Omega$ for all $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ and $y \in {\mathcal O}_d$. Thus we have $U_z\pi(s_i)U_z^*=z\pi(s_i)$ and also $U_z\pi(\tilde{s}_i)U_z^*=z\tilde{s}_i.$ By taking its restriction to $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ respectively we check that $H \subseteq \tilde{H}_{\pi} $ and $H \subseteq H_{\pi}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Gauge unitaries $U_z$ show $H\subseteq H_\pi,\tilde H_\pi$

nodes.name: Extended gauge automorphisms lie in $H$ by factoriality
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For the converse let $z \in H_{\pi}$ and we use the same symbol $\beta_z$ for the extension to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. By taking the inverse map we check easily that $\bar{z} \in H_{\pi}$ and in fact $H_{\pi}$ is a subgroup of $S^1$. Since $\lambda$ commutes with $\beta_z$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$, the canonical endomorphism $\Lambda$ defined by $\Lambda(X) = \sum_k S_kXS_k^*$ also commutes with the extension of $\beta_z$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. Note that the map $\pi(x)_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} $ for $x \in {\mathcal O}_d$ is a well defined $*$-homomorphism. Since same is true for $\bar{z}$ and $\beta_z\beta_{\bar{z}}=I$, the map is an isomorphism. Hence $\beta_z$ extends uniquely to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ commuting with the restriction of the canonical endomorphism on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{|{\mathcal H}}$. Since $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ is a factor, we conclude as in Proposition 2.5 (a) that $z \in H$. Thus $H_{\pi} \subseteq H$. As $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is also a factor, we also have $\tilde{H}_{\pi} \subseteq H$. Hence we have $H=H_{\pi}=\tilde{H}_{\pi}$ and $\{(z,z): z \in H \} \subseteq G \subseteq H \times H$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Extended gauge automorphisms lie in $H$ by factoriality

nodes.name: Quasi-equivalence (Lemma 7.11 [BJKW]) and Powers' theorem give UHF factors
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For the second part of (a) we will adopt the argument used for Proposition 2.5. To that end we first note that $\Omega$ being a cyclic vector for the representation $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ in the Hilbert space $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $, by Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] (note that the proof only needs the cyclic property ) the representation of UHF$_d$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $ is quasi-equivalent to its sub-representation on the cyclic space generated by $\Omega$. On the other hand, by our hypothesis that $\omega$ is a factor state, Power's theorem [Pow] ensures that the state $\omega'$ (i.e. the restriction of $\omega$ to ${\mathcal B}_R$ which is identified here with $\mbox{UHF}_d$ ) is also a factor state on $\mbox{UHF}_d$. Hence quasi-equivalence ensures that $\pi(I \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a factor. We also note that the argument used in Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] is symmetric i.e. same argument is also valid for $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$. Thus $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes I)''$ is also a factor. This completes the proof of (a). We have proved (b) while giving proof of (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Quasi-equivalence (Lemma 7.11 [BJKW]) and Powers' theorem give UHF factors

nodes.name: Cuntz relations preserve commutant and centre
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For $X \in {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$, as $\Lambda(X)$ commutes with $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ and $\{ S_iS^*_j: 1 \le i,j \le d \}$ we verify by Cuntz's relation that $\Lambda(X)$ is also an element in the commutant of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ once $X$ is so. It is also obvious that $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ if $X$ is so. Thus $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. For the last statement consider the map $X \rightarrow S_i^*XS_i$ on $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ which is clearly onto by Cuntz relation (3). Hence we need to show that $S^*_iXS_i$ is an element in the commutant whenever $X$ is so. To that end note that $S_i^*XS_i S_i^*YS_i=S_i^*S_iS_i^*XYS_i=S_i^*YXS_i=S^*_iYS_iS_i^*XS_i$ since $X$ commutes with $S_iS_i^*$. Thus onto property of the map ensures that $S_i^*XS_i$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. This completes the proof of (c) and (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Cuntz relations preserve commutant and centre

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant algebra I
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em One interesting problem here how to describe the von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal I}$ which consists of invariant elements of the gauge action $\{ \beta_z: z \in H \}$ in ${\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Stormer's theorem on fixed-point algebras
nodes.statement: A general result due to E. Stormer [So] says that the algebra of invariant elements is a von-Neumann algebra of type-I with centre completely atomic.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Spectral projections F_k of the gauge unitaries
nodes.statement: Here the situation is much simple because we know explicitly that ${\mathcal I}=\{U_z: z \in H \}'$ and we write spectral decomposition as \begin{equation} U_z=\sum_{ k \in \hat{H} } z^k F_k \end{equation} for $z \in H$, $\hat{H}$ is the dual group of $H$, either $\hat{H}=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Equation (30)
nodes.statement: U_z=\sum_{ k \in \hat{H} } z^k F_k
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Centre of I is generated by the F_k
nodes.statement: Thus the centre of ${\mathcal I}$ is equal to $\{F_k: k \in \hat{H} \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Centre of the amalgamated UHF algebra
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega,\psi$ be as in Proposition 3.2 with Popescu system $({\mathcal K},{\mathcal M},$ $v_k,\Omega)$ be taken as in Proposition 2.4 i.e. on support projection. Then the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is completely atomic and the element $E_0=[\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)' \vee \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$ is a minimal projection in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ and the centre is invariant for both $\Lambda$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}$. Furthermore the following holds: \vskip 1em 
oindent (a) The centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ has the following two disjoint possibilities: \vskip 1em 
oindent (i) There exists a positive integer $m \ge 1$ such that the centre is generated by the family of minimal orthogonal projections $\{ \Lambda_k(E_0): 0 \le k \le m-1 \}$ where $m \ge 1$ is the least positive integer so that $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$. In such a case $\{z: z^m = 1 \} \subseteq H$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (ii) The family of minimal nonzero orthogonal projections $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ where $E_k= \Lambda^k(E_0)$ for $k \ge 0$ and $E_k= S^*_IE_0S_I$ for $k < 0$ where $|I|=-k$ and independent of multi-index $I$ generates the centre and $H=S^1$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (b) $\Lambda(E)=	ilde{\Lambda}(E) $ for any $E$ in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ \vskip 1em 
oindent (c) If $\Lambda(E_0)=E_0$ then $E_0=1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is atomic, generated by shifts of a minimal projection $E_0$, periodic or aperiodic.

nodes.name: Proof of Centre of the amalgamated UHF algebra
nodes.statement:
Let $E' \in \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ be the projection onto the subspace generated by the vectors $\{ S_IS^*_J	ilde{S}_{I'}S^*_{J'}\Omega,\; |I|=|J|,|I'|=|J'| < \infty \}$ and $\pi_{\Omega}$ be the restriction of the representation $\pi$ of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ to the cyclic subspace ${\mathcal H}_{\Omega}$ generated by $\Omega$. Identifying ${\mathcal B}$ with $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ we check that $\pi_{\omega}$ is unitary equivalent to $\pi_{\Omega}$. Thus $\pi_{\Omega}$ is a factor representation. \vskip 1em For any projection $E$ in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, via the unitary equivalence, we note that $EE'=E'EE'$ is an element in the centre of $\pi_{\Omega}(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\omega$ being a factor state we conclude that $EE'$ is a scalar multiple of $E'$ and so we have  egin{equation} EE'=\omega(E)E' \end{equation} Thus we also have $EYE'=\omega(E)YE'$ for all $Y \in \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ and so  egin{equation} EE_0=\omega(E)E_0 \end{equation} \vskip 1em Since $EE'$ is a projection and $E' 
e 0$, we have $\omega(E)=\omega(E)^2$. Thus $\omega(E)=1$ or $0$. So, for such an element $E$, the following is true: 
oindent (i) If $E \le E_0$ then either $E=0$ or $E=E_0$ i.e. $E_0$ is a minimal projection in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ 
oindent (ii) $\omega(E)=1$ if and only if $E \ge E_0$ 
oindent (iii) $\omega(E)=0$ if and only if $EE_0=0$. \vskip 1em As $\Lambda(E_0)$ is a projection in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by our last proposition i.e. Proposition 3.2 (c), we have either $\omega(\Lambda(E_0))=1$ or $0$. Since $\Lambda(E_0) 
eq 0$ by the injective property of the endomorphism, we have either $\Lambda(E_0) \ge E_0$ or $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$. In case $\Lambda(E_0) \ge E_0$ we have $S^*_iE_0S_i \le S^*_i\Lambda(E_0)S_i=E_0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. If so, $S^*_iE_0S_i$ being a non-zero projection in the centre of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ (Proposition 3.2 (c) ), by (i) we have $E_0=\Lambda(E_0)$. Thus we have either $\Lambda(E_0)=E_0$ or $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$. \vskip 1em If $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$, we have $\Lambda(E_0) \le I-E_0$ and by Cuntz's relation we check that $E_0 \le I - S^*_iE_0S_i$ and $S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_j \le I- S^*_jE_0S_j$ for all $1 \le i,j \le d$. So we also have $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0 \le E_0- E_0S^*_jE_0S_jE_0=E_0$. Thus we have either $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0= 0$ or $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0=E_0$ as $S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_j$ is an element in the centre by Proposition 3.2 (c). So either we have $\Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^2(E_0) \le E_0$. $\Lambda$ being an injective map we either have $\Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^2(E_0)= E_0.$ \vskip 1em More generally we check that if $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0, \Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0,..\Lambda^k(E_0)E_0=0$ for some $k \ge 1$ then either $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)=E_0$. To verify that first we check that in such a case $E_0 \le I- S^*_IE_0S_I$ for all $|I|=n$ and then following the same steps as before to check that $S^*_iS^*_IE_0S_IS_i \le I-S^*E_0S_i$ for all $i$. Thus we have $E_0S^*_iS^*_IE_0S_IS_iE_0 \le E_0$ and arguing as before we complete the proof of the claim that either $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)=E_0.$ \vskip 1em We summarize now by saying that $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..,\Lambda^{m-1}(E_0)$ are mutually orthogonal projections with $m \ge 1$ possibly be infinite, if not then $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$. \vskip 1em Let $\pi_k,\;k \ge 0$ be the representation $\pi$ of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the subspace $\Lambda^k(E_0)$. The representation $\pi_0$ of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ is isomorphic to the representation $\pi$ of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to $E'$ and thus quasi-equivalent. For a general discussion on quasi-equivalence we refer to section 2.4.4 in [BR vol-1]. Since $\omega$ is a factor state, $\pi_0$ is a factor representation. We claim now that each $\pi_k$ is a factor representation. We fix any $k \ge 1$ and let $X$ be an element in the centre of $\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$. Then for any $|I|=k$, $S^*_IE_kS_I=E_0$ and so $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in the centre of $\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$ by Proposition 3.2 (d). Further $S_I^*XS_I= S^*_IXS_IS^*_JS_J = S^*_JXS_J$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation, we have $S^*_IXS_I= c E_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of the multi-index we choose $|I|=k$. Hence $c \Lambda_k(E_0) = \sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IXS_IS_J^*=\sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IS_IS_J^*X= X$ as $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)$. Thus for each $k \ge 1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation as $\pi_0$ is so. \vskip 1em We also note that $\Lambda(E_0)	ilde{\Lambda}(E_0) 
eq 0$. Otherwise we have $<S_i\Omega,	ilde{S}_j\Omega>=0$ for all $i,j$ and so $<\Omega,	ilde{S}_jS^*_i\Omega>=0$ for all $i,j$ as $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. However $	ilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and $\sum_i 	ilde{S}_i	ilde{S}^*_i=1$ which leads a contradiction. Hence $\Lambda(E_0)	ilde{\Lambda}(E_0) 
eq 0$. As $\pi$ restricted to $\Lambda(E_0)$ is a factor state and both $\Lambda(E_0)$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}(E_0)$ are elements in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF})''$, by Proposition 3.2 (d), we conclude that $\Lambda(E_0)=	ilde{\Lambda}(E_0).$ Using the commuting property of the endomorphisms $\Lambda$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}$, we verify by a simple induction method that $\Lambda^k(E_0) = 	ilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ for all $k \ge 1$. Thus the sequence of orthogonal projections $E_0, 	ilde{\Lambda}(E_0),...$, are also periodic with same period or aperiodic according as the sequence of orthogonal projections $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),...$ is. \vskip 1em If $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$ for some $m \ge 1$ then we check that $\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} \Lambda^k(E_0)$ is a $\Lambda$ and as well $	ilde{\Lambda}$-invariant projection and thus equal to $1$ by the cyclic property of $\Omega$ for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes 	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. In such a case we set $V_z=\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} z^kE_k$ for $z \in S^1$ for which $z^m=1$ and check that $\Lambda(V_z)= \sum_{0 \le k \le m-1}z^k\Lambda(E_k)=\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} z^k E_{k+1}=  ar{z} V_z$ where $E_m=E_0$ and so by the Cuntz relations we have $V^*_zS_iV_z=  ar{z}S_i$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Following the same steps we also have $	ilde{\Lambda}(V_z)= ar{z}V_z$ and so $V^*_z	ilde{S}_iV^*_z= ar{z}	ilde{S}_i$ for $ 1 \le i \le d$. Thus $V_z=U_z$ for all $z \in H_0 = \{z: z^m=1 \} \subseteq H$. \vskip 1em Now we consider the case where $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..\Lambda^k(E_0),..$ is a sequence of aperiodic orthogonal projections. We extend the family of projections $\{E_k:\;k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ to all integers by $$E_k=\Lambda^k(E_0)\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\; k \ge 1$$ and $$E_k = S^*_IE_0S_I\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\;k \le 1,\;\;\mbox{where}\;\; |I|=-k$$ We claim that the definition of $\{ E_k;\;k \le -1 \}$ does depends only on length of the multi-index $I$ that we choose. We may choose any other $J$ so that $|J|=|I|$ and check the following identity: $$S^*_IE_0S_I = S^*_IE_0S_IS^*_JS_J=S^*_IS_IS^*_JE_0S_J=S^*_JE_0S_J$$ where $E_0$, being an element in the centre of $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ as $|I|=|J|$. Further $\Lambda^k(E_0)=	ilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ ensures that $S_I	ilde{S}_J^*$ commutes with $E_0$ for all $|I|=|J|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Hence we also have $$E_{-k}=S^*_IE_0S_I	ilde{S}^*_J	ilde{S}_J=	ilde{S}^*_JE_0	ilde{S}_J$$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Now we claim that $$\Lambda(E_k) = 	ilde{\Lambda}(E_k) = E_{k+1}$$ for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. For $k \ge 0$ we have nothing to prove. For $k \le -1$ we check that the following steps $$\Lambda(S^*_IE_0S_I)$$ $$=\sum_j S_jS^*_iS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}S_iS_j^*$$ $$=\sum_jS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'} S_jS^*_iS_iS_j^* = S^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}$$ where we have $I=(I',i)$ and used the fact that elements $S_jS^*_i$ commutes with $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$, which are elements in the centre of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For a proof that $	ilde{\Lambda}(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ we may follow the same steps as $E_k=	ilde{S}^*_IX	ilde{S}_I$ where $|I|=-k$ and $k \le -1$. \vskip 1em We also claim that $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ is an orthogonal family of non-zero projections. To that end we choose any two elements say $E_k,E_m,\;k 
e m$ and use endomorphism $\Lambda^n$ for $n$ large enough so that both $n+k \ge 0 , n+m \ge 0$ to conclude that $\Lambda^n(E_kE_m) = E_{k+n}E_{k+m}=0$ as $k+n 
e k+m$. $\Lambda$ being an injective map we get the required orthogonal property. Thus $\sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} E_k$ being an invariant projection for both $\Lambda$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}$ we get by cyclic property of $\Omega$ that $\sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} E_k=I$. Let $\pi_k,\; k \le -1$ be the representation $\pi$ of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the subspace $E_k$. Going along the same line as above, we verify that for each $k \le -1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$. We also set $V_z= \sum_{-\infty < k < \infty} z^k E_k$ for all $z \in S^1$ and check that $\Lambda(V_z)= ar{z}V_z$ and also $	ilde{\Lambda}(V_z)= ar{z}V_z$. Hence $S^1=H$ as $H$ is a closed subset of $S^1$. This completes the proof of (a). Proof of (b) and (c) are now simple consequence of the proof of (a).

nodes.statement_short: Factor-state minimality of $E_0$ and Cuntz relations give periodic or aperiodic orthogonal shifts of $E_0$.

Identifying ${\mathcal B}$ with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ we check that $\pi_{\omega}$ is unitary equivalent to $\pi_{\Omega}$. Thus $\pi_{\Omega}$ is a factor representation.

nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For any projection $E$ in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, via the unitary equivalence, we note that $EE'=E'EE'$ is an element in the centre of $\pi_{\Omega}(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\omega$ being a factor state we conclude that $EE'$ is a scalar multiple of $E'$ and so we have \begin{equation} EE'=\omega(E)E' \end{equation} Thus we also have $EYE'=\omega(E)YE'$ for all $Y \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ and so \begin{equation} EE_0=\omega(E)E_0 \end{equation}

nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Since $EE'$ is a projection and $E' \ne 0$, we have $\omega(E)=\omega(E)^2$. Thus $\omega(E)=1$ or $0$. So, for such an element $E$, the following is true:

nodes.statement: (i) If $E \le E_0$ then either $E=0$ or $E=E_0$ i.e. $E_0$ is a minimal projection in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ \noindent

nodes.name: Dichotomy for $\Lambda(E_0)$ via Proposition 3.2 (c)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em As $\Lambda(E_0)$ is a projection in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by our last proposition i.e. Proposition 3.2 (c), we have either $\omega(\Lambda(E_0))=1$ or $0$. Since $\Lambda(E_0) \neq 0$ by the injective property of the endomorphism, we have either $\Lambda(E_0) \ge E_0$ or $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$. In case $\Lambda(E_0) \ge E_0$ we have $S^*_iE_0S_i \le S^*_i\Lambda(E_0)S_i=E_0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. If so, $S^*_iE_0S_i$ being a non-zero projection in the centre of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ (Proposition 3.2 (c) ), by (i) we have $E_0=\Lambda(E_0)$. Thus we have either $\Lambda(E_0)=E_0$ or $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Dichotomy for $\Lambda(E_0)$ via Proposition 3.2 (c)

nodes.name: Dichotomy for $\Lambda^2(E_0)$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em If $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$, we have $\Lambda(E_0) \le I-E_0$ and by Cuntz's relation we check that $E_0 \le I - S^*_iE_0S_i$ and $S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_j \le I- S^*_jE_0S_j$ for all $1 \le i,j \le d$. So we also have $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0 \le E_0- E_0S^*_jE_0S_jE_0=E_0$. Thus we have either $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0= 0$ or $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0=E_0$ as $S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_j$ is an element in the centre by Proposition 3.2 (c). So either we have $\Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^2(E_0) \le E_0$. $\Lambda$ being an injective map we either have $\Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^2(E_0)= E_0.$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Dichotomy for $\Lambda^2(E_0)$

nodes.name: Inductive dichotomy for $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em More generally we check that if $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0, \Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0,..\Lambda^k(E_0)E_0=0$ for some $k \ge 1$ then either $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)=E_0$. To verify that first we check that in such a case $E_0 \le I- S^*_IE_0S_I$ for all $|I|=n$ and then following the same steps as before to check that $S^*_iS^*_IE_0S_IS_i \le I-S^*E_0S_i$ for all $i$. Thus we have $E_0S^*_iS^*_IE_0S_IS_iE_0 \le E_0$ and arguing as before we complete the proof of the claim that either $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)=E_0.$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Inductive dichotomy for $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)$

nodes.name: Shifts of $E_0$ are orthogonal until periodic
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We summarize now by saying that $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..,\Lambda^{m-1}(E_0)$ are mutually orthogonal projections with $m \ge 1$ possibly be infinite, if not then $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Shifts of $E_0$ are orthogonal until periodic

nodes.name: Each restricted representation $\pi_k$ is a factor representation
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let $\pi_k,\;k \ge 0$ be the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the subspace $\Lambda^k(E_0)$. The representation $\pi_0$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ is isomorphic to the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to $E'$ and thus quasi-equivalent. For a general discussion on quasi-equivalence we refer to section 2.4.4 in [BR vol-1]. Since $\omega$ is a factor state, $\pi_0$ is a factor representation. We claim now that each $\pi_k$ is a factor representation. We fix any $k \ge 1$ and let $X$ be an element in the centre of $\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$. Then for any $|I|=k$, $S^*_IE_kS_I=E_0$ and so $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in the centre of $\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$ by Proposition 3.2 (d). Further $S_I^*XS_I= S^*_IXS_IS^*_JS_J = S^*_JXS_J$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation, we have $S^*_IXS_I= c E_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of the multi-index we choose $|I|=k$. Hence $c \Lambda_k(E_0) = \sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IXS_IS_J^*=\sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IS_IS_J^*X= X$ as $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)$. Thus for each $k \ge 1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation as $\pi_0$ is so.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Each restricted representation $\pi_k$ is a factor representation

nodes.name: Define $\pi_k$; $\pi_0$ is a factor representation
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Let $\pi_k,\;k \ge 0$ be the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the subspace $\Lambda^k(E_0)$. The representation $\pi_0$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ is isomorphic to the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to $E'$ and thus quasi-equivalent. For a general discussion on quasi-equivalence we refer to section 2.4.4 in [BR vol-1]. Since $\omega$ is a factor state, $\pi_0$ is a factor representation.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define $\pi_k$; $\pi_0$ is a factor representation

nodes.name: Claim: every $\pi_k$ is a factor representation
nodes.statement: We claim now that each $\pi_k$ is a factor representation. We fix any $k \ge 1$ and let $X$ be an element in the centre of $\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$. Then for any $|I|=k$, $S^*_IE_kS_I=E_0$ and so $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in the centre of $\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$ by Proposition 3.2 (d). Further $S_I^*XS_I= S^*_IXS_IS^*_JS_J = S^*_JXS_J$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation, we have $S^*_IXS_I= c E_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of the multi-index we choose $|I|=k$. Hence $c \Lambda_k(E_0) = \sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IXS_IS_J^*=\sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IS_IS_J^*X= X$ as $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)$. Thus for each $k \ge 1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation as $\pi_0$ is so.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Claim: every $\pi_k$ is a factor representation

nodes.name: Pull central elements back to $\pi_0$ via Proposition 3.2 (d)
nodes.statement: We fix any $k \ge 1$ and let $X$ be an element in the centre of $\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$. Then for any $|I|=k$, $S^*_IE_kS_I=E_0$ and so $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in the centre of $\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$ by Proposition 3.2 (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Pull central elements back to $\pi_0$ via Proposition 3.2 (d)

nodes.name: The pulled-back element is scalar, so $X$ is scalar on $E_k$
nodes.statement: Further $S_I^*XS_I= S^*_IXS_IS^*_JS_J = S^*_JXS_J$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation, we have $S^*_IXS_I= c E_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of the multi-index we choose $|I|=k$. Hence $c \Lambda_k(E_0) = \sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IXS_IS_J^*=\sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IS_IS_J^*X= X$ as $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)$. Thus for each $k \ge 1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation as $\pi_0$ is so.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The pulled-back element is scalar, so $X$ is scalar on $E_k$

nodes.name: $\Lambda$ and $\tilde\Lambda$ agree on the shifts of $E_0$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We also note that $\Lambda(E_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0) \neq 0$. Otherwise we have $<S_i\Omega,\tilde{S}_j\Omega>=0$ for all $i,j$ and so $<\Omega,\tilde{S}_jS^*_i\Omega>=0$ for all $i,j$ as $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. However $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and $\sum_i \tilde{S}_i\tilde{S}^*_i=1$ which leads a contradiction. Hence $\Lambda(E_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0) \neq 0$. As $\pi$ restricted to $\Lambda(E_0)$ is a factor state and both $\Lambda(E_0)$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0)$ are elements in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF})''$, by Proposition 3.2 (d), we conclude that $\Lambda(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0).$ Using the commuting property of the endomorphisms $\Lambda$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}$, we verify by a simple induction method that $\Lambda^k(E_0) = \tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ for all $k \ge 1$. Thus the sequence of orthogonal projections $E_0, \tilde{\Lambda}(E_0),...$, are also periodic with same period or aperiodic according as the sequence of orthogonal projections $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),...$ is.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $\Lambda$ and $\tilde\Lambda$ agree on the shifts of $E_0$

nodes.name: Periodic case: $V_z$ implements gauge, so $m$-th roots lie in $H$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em If $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$ for some $m \ge 1$ then we check that $\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} \Lambda^k(E_0)$ is a $\Lambda$ and as well $\tilde{\Lambda}$-invariant projection and thus equal to $1$ by the cyclic property of $\Omega$ for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. In such a case we set $V_z=\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} z^kE_k$ for $z \in S^1$ for which $z^m=1$ and check that $\Lambda(V_z)= \sum_{0 \le k \le m-1}z^k\Lambda(E_k)=\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} z^k E_{k+1}= \bar{z} V_z$ where $E_m=E_0$ and so by the Cuntz relations we have $V^*_zS_iV_z= \bar{z}S_i$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Following the same steps we also have $\tilde{\Lambda}(V_z)=\bar{z}V_z$ and so $V^*_z\tilde{S}_iV^*_z=\bar{z}\tilde{S}_i$ for $ 1 \le i \le d$. Thus $V_z=U_z$ for all $z \in H_0 = \{z: z^m=1 \} \subseteq H$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Periodic case: $V_z$ implements gauge, so $m$-th roots lie in $H$

nodes.name: Aperiodic case: extend $E_k$ to all integers
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we consider the case where $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..\Lambda^k(E_0),..$ is a sequence of aperiodic orthogonal projections. We extend the family of projections $\{E_k:\;k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ to all integers by $$E_k=\Lambda^k(E_0)\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\; k \ge 1$$ and $$E_k = S^*_IE_0S_I\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\;k \le 1,\;\;\mbox{where}\;\; |I|=-k$$ We claim that the definition of $\{ E_k;\;k \le -1 \}$ does depends only on length of the multi-index $I$ that we choose. We may choose any other $J$ so that $|J|=|I|$ and check the following identity: $$S^*_IE_0S_I = S^*_IE_0S_IS^*_JS_J=S^*_IS_IS^*_JE_0S_J=S^*_JE_0S_J$$ where $E_0$, being an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ as $|I|=|J|$. Further $\Lambda^k(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ ensures that $S_I\tilde{S}_J^*$ commutes with $E_0$ for all $|I|=|J|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Hence we also have $$E_{-k}=S^*_IE_0S_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JE_0\tilde{S}_J$$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Now we claim that $$\Lambda(E_k) = \tilde{\Lambda}(E_k) = E_{k+1}$$ for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. For $k \ge 0$ we have nothing to prove. For $k \le -1$ we check that the following steps $$\Lambda(S^*_IE_0S_I)$$ $$=\sum_j S_jS^*_iS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}S_iS_j^*$$ $$=\sum_jS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'} S_jS^*_iS_iS_j^* = S^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}$$ where we have $I=(I',i)$ and used the fact that elements $S_jS^*_i$ commutes with $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$, which are elements in the centre of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For a proof that $\tilde{\Lambda}(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ we may follow the same steps as $E_k=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$ where $|I|=-k$ and $k \le -1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Aperiodic case: extend $E_k$ to all integers

nodes.name: Define $E_k$ for negative $k$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we consider the case where $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..\Lambda^k(E_0),..$ is a sequence of aperiodic orthogonal projections. We extend the family of projections $\{E_k:\;k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ to all integers by $$E_k=\Lambda^k(E_0)\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\; k \ge 1$$ and $$E_k = S^*_IE_0S_I\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\;k \le 1,\;\;\mbox{where}\;\; |I|=-k$$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define $E_k$ for negative $k$

nodes.name: Claim: $E_{-k}$ is independent of the multi-index
nodes.statement: We claim that the definition of $\{ E_k;\;k \le -1 \}$ does depends only on length of the multi-index $I$ that we choose. We may choose any other $J$ so that $|J|=|I|$ and check the following identity: $$S^*_IE_0S_I = S^*_IE_0S_IS^*_JS_J=S^*_IS_IS^*_JE_0S_J=S^*_JE_0S_J$$ where $E_0$, being an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ as $|I|=|J|$. Further $\Lambda^k(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ ensures that $S_I\tilde{S}_J^*$ commutes with $E_0$ for all $|I|=|J|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Hence we also have $$E_{-k}=S^*_IE_0S_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JE_0\tilde{S}_J$$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$ and $k \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $E_{-k}$ is independent of the multi-index

nodes.name: Centrality of $E_0$ gives index independence
nodes.statement: We may choose any other $J$ so that $|J|=|I|$ and check the following identity: $$S^*_IE_0S_I = S^*_IE_0S_IS^*_JS_J=S^*_IS_IS^*_JE_0S_J=S^*_JE_0S_J$$ where $E_0$, being an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ as $|I|=|J|$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Centrality of $E_0$ gives index independence

nodes.name: Same formula with $\tilde S$
nodes.statement: Further $\Lambda^k(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ ensures that $S_I\tilde{S}_J^*$ commutes with $E_0$ for all $|I|=|J|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Hence we also have $$E_{-k}=S^*_IE_0S_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JE_0\tilde{S}_J$$ for all $|J|=|I|=k$ and $k \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Same formula with $\tilde S$

nodes.name: $\Lambda(E_k)=\tilde\Lambda(E_k)=E_{k+1}$
nodes.statement: Now we claim that $$\Lambda(E_k) = \tilde{\Lambda}(E_k) = E_{k+1}$$ for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. For $k \ge 0$ we have nothing to prove. For $k \le -1$ we check that the following steps $$\Lambda(S^*_IE_0S_I)$$ $$=\sum_j S_jS^*_iS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}S_iS_j^*$$ $$=\sum_jS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'} S_jS^*_iS_iS_j^* = S^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}$$ where we have $I=(I',i)$ and used the fact that elements $S_jS^*_i$ commutes with $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$, which are elements in the centre of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For a proof that $\tilde{\Lambda}(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ we may follow the same steps as $E_k=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$ where $|I|=-k$ and $k \le -1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $\Lambda(E_k)=\tilde\Lambda(E_k)=E_{k+1}$

nodes.name: Orthogonality, completeness and $H=S^1$; conclude (a)-(c)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We also claim that $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ is an orthogonal family of non-zero projections. To that end we choose any two elements say $E_k,E_m,\;k \ne m$ and use endomorphism $\Lambda^n$ for $n$ large enough so that both $n+k \ge 0 , n+m \ge 0$ to conclude that $\Lambda^n(E_kE_m) = E_{k+n}E_{k+m}=0$ as $k+n \ne k+m$. $\Lambda$ being an injective map we get the required orthogonal property. Thus $\sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} E_k$ being an invariant projection for both $\Lambda$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}$ we get by cyclic property of $\Omega$ that $\sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} E_k=I$. Let $\pi_k,\; k \le -1$ be the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the subspace $E_k$. Going along the same line as above, we verify that for each $k \le -1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$. We also set $V_z= \sum_{-\infty < k < \infty} z^k E_k$ for all $z \in S^1$ and check that $\Lambda(V_z)=\bar{z}V_z$ and also $\tilde{\Lambda}(V_z)=\bar{z}V_z$. Hence $S^1=H$ as $H$ is a closed subset of $S^1$. This completes the proof of (a). Proof of (b) and (c) are now simple consequence of the proof of (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality, completeness and $H=S^1$; conclude (a)-(c)

nodes.name: Algebra I_0
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em It is clear that ${\mathcal I}$ contains ${\mathcal I}_0:=^{\mbox{def}} \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'' \vee \{U_z: z \in H \}''$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: I is contained in the algebra generated by the UHF algebra and its commutant
nodes.statement: By the last proposition the centre of ${\mathcal I}$, which is equal to $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$, contains the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ and thus by taking the commutant we also have ${\mathcal I} \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\vee \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Restricted representations pi'_k
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For each $k \in \hat{H}$, let $\pi'_k$ be the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to $F_k$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Each pi'_k is pure if pi'_0 is pure
nodes.statement: We claim that each $\pi'_k$ is pure if $\pi'_0$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Proof that each pi'_k is pure
nodes.statement: Fix any $k \in \hat{H}$ and let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi'_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ then $S^*_IF_kS_I = S^*_I\Lambda^k(F_0)S_I = F_0$ as $S^*_JS_I$ commutes with $F_0$ for $|I|=|J|=k$ and further for any $|I|=|J|$, $S_I^*XS_IS_J^*S_J=S_I^*S_IS_J^*XS_J=S^*_JXS_J$ as $X$ commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ with $|I|=|J|$. Thus by Proposition 3.2 (c) $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in commutant of $\pi'_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ for any $|I|=k$ and thus $S_I^*XS_I= c F_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of $|I|=k$ as $\pi'_0$ is pure. We use the commuting property of $X$ with $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ to conclude that $X = c \Lambda^k(E_0)$ for some scalar $c$. If $k \le -1$ we employ the same method but with the endomorphism $\Lambda^{-k}$ so that $\Lambda^{-k}(X)$ is an element in the commutant of $\pi'_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. Thus $\sum_{I:|I|=-k }S_IXS^*_I = c I$ and by the injective property of the endomorphism we get $X$ is a scalar. Thus we conclude that each $\pi'_k$ is pure if $\pi'_0$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Pull back commutant elements by $X\mapsto S_I^*XS_I$ (or push by $\Lambda^{-k}$) to the pure $\pi'_0$.

nodes.name: Pull back $X$ by $S_I^*\cdot S_I$
nodes.statement: Fix any $k \in \hat{H}$ and let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi'_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ then $S^*_IF_kS_I = S^*_I\Lambda^k(F_0)S_I = F_0$ as $S^*_JS_I$ commutes with $F_0$ for $|I|=|J|=k$ and further for any $|I|=|J|$, $S_I^*XS_IS_J^*S_J=S_I^*S_IS_J^*XS_J=S^*_JXS_J$ as $X$ commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ with $|I|=|J|$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Pull back $X$ by $S_I^*\cdot S_I$

nodes.name: Purity of $\pi'_0$ makes $X$ scalar for $k\ge0$
nodes.statement: Thus by Proposition 3.2 (c) $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in commutant of $\pi'_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ for any $|I|=k$ and thus $S_I^*XS_I= c F_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of $|I|=k$ as $\pi'_0$ is pure. We use the commuting property of $X$ with $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ to conclude that $X = c \Lambda^k(E_0)$ for some scalar $c$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Purity of $\pi'_0$ makes $X$ scalar for $k\ge0$

nodes.name: Negative $k$ via $\Lambda^{-k}$
nodes.statement: If $k \le -1$ we employ the same method but with the endomorphism $\Lambda^{-k}$ so that $\Lambda^{-k}(X)$ is an element in the commutant of $\pi'_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. Thus $\sum_{I:|I|=-k }S_IXS^*_I = c I$ and by the injective property of the endomorphism we get $X$ is a scalar. Thus we conclude that each $\pi'_k$ is pure if $\pi'_0$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Negative $k$ via $\Lambda^{-k}$

nodes.name: pi_k is quasi-equivalent to pi'_k
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Next we claim that for each fixed $k \in \hat{H_0}$, the representation $\pi_k$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ defined in the proof of Proposition 3.3 is quasi-equivalent to representation $\pi'_k$ ( here we recall $\hat{H_0} \subseteq \hat{H}$ as $H_0 \subseteq H$ ).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Proof that pi_k is quasi-equivalent to pi'_k
nodes.statement: That $\pi'_0$ is quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0$ follows as they are isomorphic by construction. In the proof of Proposition 3.3 we defined representation $\pi_k$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ for all $k \in \hat{H}_0$ associated with minimal projections $\{E_k: k \in \hat{H}_0 \}$. More generally for any $k \in \hat{H}$, we denote $\pi_k$ for the restriction of $\pi$ to the minimal central projections $E_k$ on the subspace span by $\{\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'f: \forall \;\; f\;\; \in {\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}, \;\;F_kf=f \}$. So each $E_k$ is a minimal central element containing $F_k$. However two such elements i.e. $E_k$ and $E_j$ are either equal or mutually orthogonal being minimal. Thus $\{E_k: k \in \hat{H} \} = \{E_k: k \in \hat{H}_0 \}$ and quasi-equivalence follows as $\pi_k$ is isomorphic with $\pi'_k$ for all $k \in \hat{H}_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Minimal central projections containing $F_k$ coincide with the $E_k$, so the restrictions are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Base case $k=0$ and recall the $E_k$
nodes.statement: That $\pi'_0$ is quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0$ follows as they are isomorphic by construction. In the proof of Proposition 3.3 we defined representation $\pi_k$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ for all $k \in \hat{H}_0$ associated with minimal projections $\{E_k: k \in \hat{H}_0 \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Base case $k=0$ and recall the $E_k$

nodes.name: Minimal central projections containing $F_k$
nodes.statement: More generally for any $k \in \hat{H}$, we denote $\pi_k$ for the restriction of $\pi$ to the minimal central projections $E_k$ on the subspace span by $\{\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'f: \forall \;\; f\;\; \in {\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}, \;\;F_kf=f \}$. So each $E_k$ is a minimal central element containing $F_k$. However two such elements i.e. $E_k$ and $E_j$ are either equal or mutually orthogonal being minimal.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Minimal central projections containing $F_k$

nodes.name: Quasi-equivalence

nodes.name: Proof that F'_0 equals F_0 for pure omega
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em First we consider the case when $H=\{z: z^n=1\}$. Projections $\Lambda(F'_0)$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$ are elements in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ by Proposition 3.3. The representation $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ restricted to both the projections $\Lambda(F'_0),\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$ are pure as well. A pull back by the map $X \rightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ with any $1 \le i \le d$ will do the job for the projection $\Lambda(F'_0)$. Thus $\Lambda(F'_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)\Lambda(F'_0) = c \Lambda(F'_0)$ for some scalar. By pulling back with the action $X \rightarrow S^*_i X S_i$ we get $F'_0 S^*_i\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)S_i F'_0 = cF'_0$ and so $$c=<\Omega,S^*_i\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)S_i\Omega>$$ $$=\sum_k <\Omega,S_k S^*_iF'_0S_iS^*_k\Omega>$$ as $\tilde{S}^*_k\Omega=S^*_k\Omega$ and further $F'_0$ commutes with $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)$ and thus $$c=\sum_k <\Omega, S_k S_k^*\Omega>=1$$ This shows that $\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0) \ge \Lambda(F'_0)$. Interchanging the role of $\Lambda$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}$ we conclude that $\Lambda(F'_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$. Now it essentially follows along the same line $\Lambda^k(F'_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(F'_0)$ for all $k \ge 1$. By Proposition 2.5 we also note that $$\Lambda^n(F'_0)=F'_0=\tilde{\Lambda}^n(F_0)$$ as $H=\{z : z^n =1 \}$. Thus $F'=\sum_{0 \le k \le n-1}\Lambda(F'_0)$ is a $\Lambda$ and as well $\tilde{\Lambda}$ invariant projection. Since $F'\Omega=\Omega$ we conclude by the cyclic property of $\Omega$ for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ that $F'=1$. Since $\Lambda^k(F'_0) \le F_k$ and $\sum_k F_k=1 $, we conclude that $\Lambda^k(F_0)=F_k$. In such a case we may check that $$F_k = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S^*_I\Omega: |I|=n-k]$$ for $1 \le k \le n-1$. \vskip 1em Similarly in case $H=S^1$ and $\omega$ is pure we also have $F_0=F'_0$ and for $k \ge 1$ $$F_k=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S_I\Omega: |I|= k]$$ $$F_{-k}=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S^*_I\Omega: |I|=k]$$ Thus we have got an explicit description of the complete atomic centre of ${\mathcal I}$ when $\omega$ is a pure state.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on $H$ finite or $S^1$: $\Lambda$ and $\tilde\Lambda$ agree on $F'_0$, and the shifted projections sum to $1$.

nodes.name: Finite $H$: $\Lambda(F'_0)=\tilde\Lambda(F'_0)$ and shifts sum to $1$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em First we consider the case when $H=\{z: z^n=1\}$. Projections $\Lambda(F'_0)$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$ are elements in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ by Proposition 3.3. The representation $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ restricted to both the projections $\Lambda(F'_0),\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$ are pure as well. A pull back by the map $X \rightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ with any $1 \le i \le d$ will do the job for the projection $\Lambda(F'_0)$. Thus $\Lambda(F'_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)\Lambda(F'_0) = c \Lambda(F'_0)$ for some scalar. By pulling back with the action $X \rightarrow S^*_i X S_i$ we get $F'_0 S^*_i\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)S_i F'_0 = cF'_0$ and so $$c=<\Omega,S^*_i\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)S_i\Omega>$$ $$=\sum_k <\Omega,S_k S^*_iF'_0S_iS^*_k\Omega>$$ as $\tilde{S}^*_k\Omega=S^*_k\Omega$ and further $F'_0$ commutes with $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)$ and thus $$c=\sum_k <\Omega, S_k S_k^*\Omega>=1$$ This shows that $\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0) \ge \Lambda(F'_0)$. Interchanging the role of $\Lambda$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}$ we conclude that $\Lambda(F'_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$. Now it essentially follows along the same line $\Lambda^k(F'_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(F'_0)$ for all $k \ge 1$. By Proposition 2.5 we also note that $$\Lambda^n(F'_0)=F'_0=\tilde{\Lambda}^n(F_0)$$ as $H=\{z : z^n =1 \}$. Thus $F'=\sum_{0 \le k \le n-1}\Lambda(F'_0)$ is a $\Lambda$ and as well $\tilde{\Lambda}$ invariant projection. Since $F'\Omega=\Omega$ we conclude by the cyclic property of $\Omega$ for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ that $F'=1$. Since $\Lambda^k(F'_0) \le F_k$ and $\sum_k F_k=1 $, we conclude that $\Lambda^k(F_0)=F_k$. In such a case we may check that $$F_k = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S^*_I\Omega: |I|=n-k]$$ for $1 \le k \le n-1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Finite $H$: $\Lambda(F'_0)=\tilde\Lambda(F'_0)$ and shifts sum to $1$

nodes.name: $H=S^1$ similarly
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Similarly in case $H=S^1$ and $\omega$ is pure we also have $F_0=F'_0$ and for $k \ge 1$ $$F_k=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S_I\Omega: |I|= k]$$ $$F_{-k}=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S^*_I\Omega: |I|=k]$$ Thus we have got an explicit description of the complete atomic centre of ${\mathcal I}$ when $\omega$ is a pure state.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $H=S^1$ similarly

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant elements and purity
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega,\psi$ and Popescu system $({\mathcal K},{\mathcal M},v_k,\Omega)$ be as in Proposition 3.3. Then 
oindent (a) $\{ eta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''$ ( as well as in $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ ) are equal to $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. 
oindent (b) ${\mathcal I}={\mathcal I}_0$ if and only if $\omega$ is pure. Further the following statements are equivalent: 
oindent (c) ${\mathcal I} = \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$; 
oindent (d) $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$; 
oindent (e) $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d )''= {\mathcal B}(	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$; \vskip 1em In such a case (i.e. if any of (c),(d) and (e) is true ) the following statements are also true: 
oindent (f) $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a type-I von-Neumann algebra with centre equal to $\{ U_z: z \in H \}''$ where $U_z$ is defined in Proposition 3.2. 
oindent (g) $\omega$ is a pure state on ${\mathcal B}$. \vskip 1em Conversely if $\omega$ is a pure state then $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a type-I von-Neumann algebra with centre equal to $\{U_z: z \in H_0 \}''$ where $H_0$ is a subgroup of $H$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Gauge-invariant elements of the half-Cuntz algebras are the UHF algebra; ${\mathcal I}={\mathcal I}_0$ iff $\omega$ is pure, plus type-I criteria.

nodes.name: Proof of Gauge-invariant elements and purity
nodes.statement: Along the same line of the proof of Proposition 2.5 (b) we get $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ where factor property of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ is crucial as in proof of Proposition 2.5 (b). Same holds for $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ as $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is a factor. Here we comment that factor property of $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ can be ensured whenever $\psi$ is an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (See Proposition 3.2 (a) ). \vskip 1em For (b) we will first prove ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ if $\omega$ is pure. As by definition ${\mathcal I}_0 \subseteq {\mathcal I}$, it is enough if we show ${\mathcal I}'_0 \subseteq {\mathcal I}'$. Let $X \in {\mathcal I}'_0$ i.e. $X$ commutes with $\{ U_z:z \in H\}''$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For each $k \in \hat{H}$, $F_kXF_k$ is an element in the commutant of $F_k\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_k$. $\omega$ being pure each representation $\pi$ restricted to $F_k$ is irreducible and thus $F_kXF_k = c_k F_k$ for some scalars $c_k$. Hence $X=\sum_k c_k F_k \in {\mathcal I}'=\{U_z: z \in H \}''$. \vskip 1em For the converse we need to show that the restriction of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ to $F'_0$ is pure. Let $X$ be an element on the subspace $F'_0$ and in the commutant of $F'_0\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F'_0$, ( which in our earlier notation $E'$ in Proposition 3.3 ). Then $X$ commutes with each $F_k$ for $k \in \hat{H}$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_k$ as $F'_0 \le F_0$ and $F_k$ are orthogonal to $F'_0$ for $k \neq 0$. So $X$ commutes with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ i.e. $X \in {\mathcal I}'_0$. By our assumption ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$, we have now $X \in {\mathcal I}'$ which is equal to $\{F_k: k \in \hat{H} \}''$ and so $X=cF_0$ for some scalar $c_0$. This shows that $F'_0=F_0$ and $\omega$ is pure. \vskip 1em (c) implies (d): $\{U_z: z \in H \}$ is a commuting family of unitaries such that $\beta_z(X)=U_zXU_z^*$ and thus by (c) $\{U_z: z \in H \}'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. Let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''$. Then $X$ commutes also with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and thus $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by (c). Hence $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ and so $X=\sum_k c_kE_k$ where $E_k$ are the minimal projections in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ given in Proposition 3.3. However $X$ also commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ by our assumption (c) and $\Lambda(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ for $k \in \hat{H}$. So $c_k=c_{k+1}$ and $X$ is a scalar multiple of unit operator. Hence (d) follows from (c). Along the same line we prove (c) implies (e). For a proof for (d) implies (c) and (e) implies (c), we simply apply (a). \vskip 1em Now we will prove (f) and (g). That $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a type-I von-Neumann algebra ( with completely atomic centre ) follows by a theorem of [So] once we use (c). In the proof of Proposition 3.3 we have proved that the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is $\{U_z: z \in H_0 \}''$ where $H_0 \subseteq H$. For equality in the present situation we simply use (c), as $\beta_w(U_z)=U_z$ for all $w,z \in H$, to conclude that $U_z$ is in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. \vskip 1em If (c) holds then ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ and thus (g) follows by (b). Here we will give another proof using the same idea to prove (f). Let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, where $\pi_0$ is the factor representation on the minimal central projection $E_0$ defined in Proposition 3.3. Then $X$ commutes with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and so by (c) $X$ in an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. So $X$ is in the centre of $\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation $X$ is a scalar multiple of $E_0$. Thus $\pi_0$ is an irreducible representation and so $\omega$ is pure. \vskip 1em By Proposition 3.1 we recall that $\pi'_0$ is unitary equivalent to the GNS representation of $({\mathcal B},\omega)$. Thus $\pi'_0$ is irreducible if and only if $\omega$ is pure. So for a pure state $\omega$, for each $k \in \hat{H}_0$, $\pi_k$ being quasi-equivalent to $\pi'_k$, $\pi_k$ is a type-I factor representation of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. This completes the proof.

nodes.statement_short: Spectral decomposition of the gauge unitaries and purity of each restriction $\pi'_k$.

nodes.name: Part (a) as in Proposition 2.5 (b)
nodes.statement: Along the same line of the proof of Proposition 2.5 (b) we get $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ where factor property of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ is crucial as in proof of Proposition 2.5 (b). Same holds for $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ as $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is a factor. Here we comment that factor property of $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ can be ensured whenever $\psi$ is an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (See Proposition 3.2 (a) ).
