nodes.statement_short: Part (a) as in Proposition 2.5 (b)

nodes.name: Purity implies ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For (b) we will first prove ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ if $\omega$ is pure. As by definition ${\mathcal I}_0 \subseteq {\mathcal I}$, it is enough if we show ${\mathcal I}'_0 \subseteq {\mathcal I}'$. Let $X \in {\mathcal I}'_0$ i.e. $X$ commutes with $\{ U_z:z \in H\}''$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For each $k \in \hat{H}$, $F_kXF_k$ is an element in the commutant of $F_k\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_k$. $\omega$ being pure each representation $\pi$ restricted to $F_k$ is irreducible and thus $F_kXF_k = c_k F_k$ for some scalars $c_k$. Hence $X=\sum_k c_k F_k \in {\mathcal I}'=\{U_z: z \in H \}''$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Purity implies ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$

nodes.name: ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ implies $F'_0=F_0$ and purity
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For the converse we need to show that the restriction of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ to $F'_0$ is pure. Let $X$ be an element on the subspace $F'_0$ and in the commutant of $F'_0\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F'_0$, ( which in our earlier notation $E'$ in Proposition 3.3 ). Then $X$ commutes with each $F_k$ for $k \in \hat{H}$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_k$ as $F'_0 \le F_0$ and $F_k$ are orthogonal to $F'_0$ for $k \neq 0$. So $X$ commutes with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ i.e. $X \in {\mathcal I}'_0$. By our assumption ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$, we have now $X \in {\mathcal I}'$ which is equal to $\{F_k: k \in \hat{H} \}''$ and so $X=cF_0$ for some scalar $c_0$. This shows that $F'_0=F_0$ and $\omega$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ implies $F'_0=F_0$ and purity

nodes.name: Equivalence of (c),(d),(e)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em (c) implies (d): $\{U_z: z \in H \}$ is a commuting family of unitaries such that $\beta_z(X)=U_zXU_z^*$ and thus by (c) $\{U_z: z \in H \}'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. Let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''$. Then $X$ commutes also with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and thus $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by (c). Hence $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ and so $X=\sum_k c_kE_k$ where $E_k$ are the minimal projections in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ given in Proposition 3.3. However $X$ also commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ by our assumption (c) and $\Lambda(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ for $k \in \hat{H}$. So $c_k=c_{k+1}$ and $X$ is a scalar multiple of unit operator. Hence (d) follows from (c). Along the same line we prove (c) implies (e). For a proof for (d) implies (c) and (e) implies (c), we simply apply (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Equivalence of (c),(d),(e)

nodes.name: Type-I by Stormer's theorem; centre is $\{U_z\}''$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we will prove (f) and (g). That $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a type-I von-Neumann algebra ( with completely atomic centre ) follows by a theorem of [So] once we use (c). In the proof of Proposition 3.3 we have proved that the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is $\{U_z: z \in H_0 \}''$ where $H_0 \subseteq H$. For equality in the present situation we simply use (c), as $\beta_w(U_z)=U_z$ for all $w,z \in H$, to conclude that $U_z$ is in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Type-I by Stormer's theorem; centre is $\{U_z\}''$

nodes.name: Second proof of (g)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em If (c) holds then ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ and thus (g) follows by (b). Here we will give another proof using the same idea to prove (f). Let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, where $\pi_0$ is the factor representation on the minimal central projection $E_0$ defined in Proposition 3.3. Then $X$ commutes with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and so by (c) $X$ in an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. So $X$ is in the centre of $\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation $X$ is a scalar multiple of $E_0$. Thus $\pi_0$ is an irreducible representation and so $\omega$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Second proof of (g)

nodes.name: Converse: pure $\omega$ gives type-I factor restrictions
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em By Proposition 3.1 we recall that $\pi'_0$ is unitary equivalent to the GNS representation of $({\mathcal B},\omega)$. Thus $\pi'_0$ is irreducible if and only if $\omega$ is pure. So for a pure state $\omega$, for each $k \in \hat{H}_0$, $\pi_k$ being quasi-equivalent to $\pi'_k$, $\pi_k$ is a type-I factor representation of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. This completes the proof.

nodes.statement_short: Converse: pure $\omega$ gives type-I factor restrictions

nodes.name: Support projections of the dual Cuntz representations
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be an extremal translation invariant state on ${\mathcal B}$ and $\psi$ be an extremal element $\psi$ in $K_{\omega}$. We consider the Popescu elements $({\mathcal K},v_k:1 \le k \le d, {\mathcal M},\Omega)$ as in Proposition 2.4 for the dual Popescu elements and associated amalgamated representation $\pi$ of ${\mathcal O}_d \otimes 	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ as described in Proposition 3.1. Let ${\mathcal E}$ and $	ilde{{\mathcal E}}$ be the support projections of the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ respectively. Let ${\mathcal F}$ and $	ilde{{\mathcal F}}$ be the projections $[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\Omega]$ and $[\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)\Omega]$ respectively. Then the following holds: \vskip 1em 
oindent (a) $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}( 	ilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (b) $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''=\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ if and only if $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''{\mathcal E}=\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'{\mathcal E}$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (c) $Q={\mathcal E} 	ilde{{\mathcal E}}$ is the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''	ilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and also in $\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''{\mathcal E}$. Further $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} \le Q$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (d) If ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} = 	ilde{{\mathcal E}}	ilde{{\mathcal F}}$ then ${\mathcal E}=	ilde{{\mathcal F}},\;	ilde{{\mathcal E}}={\mathcal F},\;P=Q$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (e) If $P=Q$ then the following statements are true: \vskip 1em 
oindent (i) ${\mathcal M}'= 	ilde{{\mathcal M}}$ where $	ilde{{\mathcal M}} = \{ P	ilde{S}_iP: 1 \le i \le d \}''$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (ii) $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)' = \pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (f) If $P=[	ilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]$ then ${\mathcal M}'=	ilde{{\mathcal M}}$; \vskip 1em 
oindent (g) $\omega$ is pure on ${\mathcal B}$ if and only if there exists a sequence of elements $x_n \in {\mathcal M}$ such that for each $m \ge 0$ $x_{n+m}	au_n(x) ightarrow \phi(x)1$ as $n ightarrow \infty$ in strong operator topology, equivalently $\phi(	au_n(x)x_{n+m}^*x_{n+m}	au_n(y)) ightarrow \phi(x)\phi(y)$ as $n ightarrow \infty$ for all $x,y \in {\mathcal M}$ where ${\mathcal M} = \{ v_i=PS_iP: 1 \le i \le d \}''$ and $	au(x)=\sum_{1 \le k \le d}v_kxv_k^*,\;\;x \in {\mathcal M}$; Same holds true if we replace ${\mathcal M}_0$ for ${\mathcal M}$ where ${\mathcal M}_0=\{x \in {\mathcal M}:  eta_z(x)=x; z \in H \}$.

nodes.statement_short: Support-projection computations; ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{\mathcal M}$ by contradiction via a strictly ordered family of quasi-equivalent representations. Hausdorff maximality yields an impossible self-comparison.

nodes.name: Part (a) from Proposition 3.2; $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E})\uparrow I$
nodes.statement: (a) is a restatement of Proposition 3.2 (a). ${\mathcal E}$ ( $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ ) being the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ ( $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ ) and $\psi = \psi \Lambda$ we have $\Lambda({\mathcal E}) \ge {\mathcal E}$ and further we have ${\mathcal E}=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega] \ge [\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]$ and hence increasing projections in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ because $\Omega$ is cyclic for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ in ${\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ and limiting projection being in the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ as well i.e. since $\Lambda(Y)=Y$ implies $Y \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ by Cuntz relations.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Part (a) from Proposition 3.2; $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E})\uparrow I$

nodes.name: Part (b) via ${\mathcal N}_1,{\mathcal N}_2$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We set von-Neumann algebras ${\mathcal N}_1=\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'{\mathcal E}$ and ${\mathcal N}_2=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''{\mathcal E}$. By our construction we have $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'' \subseteq \pi({\mathcal O}_d)' $ and so ${\mathcal N}_2 \subseteq {\mathcal N}_1$. Since $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ in strong operator topology, two operators in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ are same if their actions are same on ${\mathcal E}$. So (b) is true.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Part (b) via ${\mathcal N}_1,{\mathcal N}_2$

nodes.name: Part (c): $Q$ is the support projection
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For (c) we note that $Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \in {\mathcal N}_2 \subseteq {\mathcal N}_1$ and claim that $Q$ is the support projection of the state $\psi$ in ${\mathcal N}_2$. To that end let $x{\mathcal E} \ge 0$ for some $x \in \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ so that $\psi(QxQ)=0$. As $\Lambda^k(x{\mathcal E}) \ge 0$ for all $k \ge 1$ and $\Lambda^k({\mathcal E}) \rightarrow I$ we conclude that $x \ge 0$. As ${\mathcal E} \Omega=\Omega$ and thus $\psi(\tilde{{\mathcal E}}x\tilde{{\mathcal E}})=\psi(QxQ)=0$, we conclude $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}x\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=0$, $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ being the support projection for $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. Hence $QxQ=0$. As $\psi(Q)=1$, we complete the proof of the claim that $Q$ is the support of $\psi$ in ${\mathcal N}_2$. Similarly $Q$ is also the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. This completes the proof of (c).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Part (c): $Q$ is the support projection

nodes.name: Part (d) by taking limits
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Thus if ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$, we get $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \Lambda^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}})$ and ${\mathcal E} \tilde{\Lambda}({\mathcal F}) = \tilde{\Lambda}(\tilde{{\mathcal E}})\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and thus taking limit we get ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. It is obvious now that $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} = {\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}}=Q$. This completes the proof of (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Part (d) by taking limits

nodes.name: Corner algebras on $Q$ are factors; $P\in{\mathcal M}^{1'}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em As ${\mathcal E} \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \in \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ we check that von-Neumann algebras ${\mathcal M}^1 = Q \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' Q$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1 = Q \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d) Q$ acting on $Q$ satisfy $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1 \subseteq {\mathcal M}^{1'}$. Now we explore that $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}})$ and note that in such a case $Q\pi( \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d )''Q$ is the set of all bounded operators on the Hilbert subspace $Q$. As ${\mathcal E} \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \in \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ we check that together ${\mathcal M}^1 = Q \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' Q$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1 = Q \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d) Q$ generate all bounded operators on $Q$. Thus both ${\mathcal M}^1$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1$ are factors. The canonical states $\psi$ on ${\mathcal M}^1$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1$ are faithful and normal. We set $l_k=QS_kQ$ and $\tilde{l}_k=Q\tilde{S}_kQ,\; 1 \le k \le d$ and recall that $v_k=PS_kP$ and $\tilde{v}_k=P\tilde{S}_kP,\; 1 \le k \le d$. We note that $Pl_kP=v_k$ and $P\tilde{l}_kP = \tilde{v}_k$ where we recall that, by our construction, $P$ is the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{|}[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)\Omega]$. $Q$ being the support projection of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$, by Theorem 2.4 applied to Cuntz elements $\{S_i\tilde{E}: 1 \le i \le d \}$, $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ is order isomorphic to ${\mathcal M}^{1'}$ via the map $X \rightarrow QXQ$. As the projection ${\mathcal F}=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\Omega] \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$, we check that the element $Q{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}Q \in {\mathcal M}^{1'}$. However $Q{\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal E}}Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}{\mathcal E}=QPQ=P$ and thus $P \in {\mathcal M}^{1'}$. We also check that ${\mathcal M}^1\Omega={\mathcal M}^1P\Omega=P{\mathcal M}^1\Omega={\mathcal M} \Omega$ and thus $P=[{\mathcal M}^1\Omega]$. We set $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ for the von-Neumann algebra generated by $\{\tilde{v}_k:\; 1 \le k \le d \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Corner algebras on $Q$ are factors; $P\in{\mathcal M}^{1'}$

nodes.name: Under $P=Q$ reduce (e) to proving (i)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em So far our analysis did not use the hypothesis on statement (e) i.e. $P=Q$. For $P=Q$, we have ${\mathcal M}^1={\mathcal M}$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. By order isomorphic property we get (i) is equivalent to $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \pi({\mathcal O}_d)' \tilde{{\mathcal E}} = \tilde{{\mathcal E}} \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and taking commutant again we get $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal E}} = \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. Now we invoke the first part of the argument changing the role or using the endomorphism $\tilde{\Lambda}$ we conclude that $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$. This completes the proof of (e) provided we find a independent proof for (i) which is not so evident and this crucial point was not noticed in the proof given for Lemma 7.8 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Under $P=Q$ reduce (e) to proving (i)

nodes.name: $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating for $\tilde{\mathcal M}$ and ${\mathcal M}'$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we will analyze the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ which is pure to prove (i). To that end we note since $P=Q$ by our assumption, $\Omega$ is a common cyclic and separating vector for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ and ${\mathcal M}'$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating for $\tilde{\mathcal M}$ and ${\mathcal M}'$

nodes.name: Endomorphism $\alpha$ from modular conjugations
nodes.statement: Thus we can get an endomorphism $\alpha: {\mathcal M}' \rightarrow \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ defined by $$\alpha(y)=\tilde{{\mathcal J}}{\mathcal J} y {\mathcal J} \tilde{{\mathcal J}}$$ where $\tilde{{\mathcal J}}$ is the Tomita's conjugate operator associated with the cyclic and separating vector $\Omega$ for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ ( i.e. for $y \in {\mathcal M}'$, we have ${\mathcal J} y {\mathcal J} \in {\mathcal M} \subseteq \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$ since $\tilde{{\mathcal M}} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. Since $\tilde{{\mathcal J}}\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'\tilde{{\mathcal J}}=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$, we have $\alpha(y) \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ ). We note that the general theory does not guarantee [AcC] that the endomorphism be Takesaki's canonical conditional expectation associated with $\phi$. If so then the modular automorphism group $(\sigma_t)$ of ${\mathcal M}'$ also preserves $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Thus $\sigma_z(x) \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ for $-1 \le Im(z) \le 1$ if $x$ is an analytic element in $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Thus we would have got ${\mathcal J} v_k(\delta) {\mathcal J} = \sigma_{i \over 2}(\tilde{v}_k(\delta)) \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ where $x(\delta)$ is average of $\sigma_t(x)$ with respect to Gaussian measure with variance $\delta > 0$. That $\tilde{v}_k(\delta)$ is an analytic element follows from the general Tomita-Takesaki theory [BR1]. Since $v_k(\delta) \rightarrow v_k$ in strong operator topology as $\delta \rightarrow 0$ and ${\mathcal M} = \{v_k: 1 \le k \le d \}''$ together with ${\mathcal J} {\mathcal M} {\mathcal J} = {\mathcal M}'$ we arrived at $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$. In the following we avoid this tempting route and aim to explore the general representation theory of $C^*$-algebras [BR1,chapter 2].
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Endomorphism $\alpha$ from modular conjugations

nodes.name: Assume strict inclusion; get a strictly decreasing chain of dilations
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We claim that ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Suppose not i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}} \subset {\mathcal M}'$. Then $\alpha(\tilde{{\mathcal M}})$ is a proper von-Neumann subalgebras of $\alpha({\mathcal M}') \subseteq \tilde{{\mathcal M}} $ being an into map and hence $\alpha(\tilde{{\mathcal M}})$ is a proper von-Neumann sub-algebra of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Now consider the Popescu elements $({\mathcal K},\alpha(\tilde{v}_i),\Omega)$ and its dilation as in Theorem 2.1. Then by the commutant lifting theorem applied to pairs $(\tilde{v}_i),\alpha(\tilde{v}_i)$ we find a unitary operator $U$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ so that $U\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''U^*$ is strictly contained in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ ( Without loss of generality we can take the dilated Hilbert space for $({\mathcal K},\alpha(\tilde{v}_i),\Omega)$ to be same as $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ as there exists an isomorphism preserving ${\mathcal K}$, see the remark that follows after Theorem 2.1 ). We extend $U$ to a unitary operator on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ and denote $\pi_u(x)=U \pi(x) U^*$ for $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ which is unitary equivalent to the pure representation $\pi$ and $\pi_u(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is strictly contained in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. Now $\pi_u$ is also an amalgamated representation over the subspace ${\mathcal K}$ with $P_u=Q_u$. Thus we can repeat now same procedure with $\pi_u$ and so on. Note that the process won't terminate in finite time. Our aim is to find a contradiction from this using formal set theory.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Assume strict inclusion; get a strictly decreasing chain of dilations

nodes.name: Define the class ${\mathcal P}$ and the order with condition (C1)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em To that end we use temporary notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ defined in last paragraph and $\pi$ will be used for a generic representation. Let ${\mathcal P}$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0:\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} )$ with a shift invariant vector state $\omega(x)=<\Omega,\pi(x)\Omega>$ i.e. $\omega(\pi(\theta(x))=\omega(\pi(x))$. So there exists cardinal numbers $n_{\pi},n_0(\pi)$ so that $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to $n_0(\pi)\pi_0$. Thus given an element $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ we can associate two cardinal numbers $n_{\pi}$ and $n_0(\pi)$ and without loss of generality we assume that $H_{\pi} \subseteq n_0(\pi)H_0$ and $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}=n_0(\pi)H_0.$ $\pi_0$ being a pure representation, any element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ is a type-I factor representation of $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d $. The interesting point here that $\displaystyle{\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P} }}\pi$ is also an element in ${\mathcal P}$ with associated cardinal numbers $\sum_{\pi} n_{\pi}$ and $\sum_{\pi} n_0(\pi)$. We say $(\pi_1,H_{\pi_1},\Omega^1) \prec (\pi_2,H_{\pi_2},\Omega^2)$ if there exists an isometry $U:n_{\pi_1} H_{\pi_1} \rightarrow n_{\pi_2} H_{\pi_2}$ so that \vskip 1em \noindent (C1) For each $1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} $ we have $U \Omega^1_{\alpha} = \Omega^2_{\alpha'}$ for some $1 \le \alpha' \le n_{\pi_2}$; \noindent
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define the class ${\mathcal P}$ and the order with condition (C1)

nodes.name: Condition (C2): intertwining up to a commutant projection
nodes.statement: (C2) $n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(x)E'_2 = U n_{\pi_1}\pi_1(x) U^* $ where ${\mathcal E}'_2 \in n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$; \noindent
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Condition (C2): intertwining up to a commutant projection

nodes.name: Condition (C3): strict inclusion of dual algebras
nodes.statement: (C3) $U\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''U^* \subset \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''E'_2$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Condition (C3): strict inclusion of dual algebras

nodes.name: The order is strict and transitive with infinite chains
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega) \prec (\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ contradicts (C3) as $I=E_2'$. By our starting assumption that ${\mathcal M}' \neq \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ we check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ there exists an element $\pi' \in {\mathcal P}$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus ${\mathcal P}_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The order is strict and transitive with infinite chains

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality yields a contradiction
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset ${\mathcal P}_0$ of ${\mathcal P}$. We claim that $\pi_{max}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in ${\mathcal P}_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_1,\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists an element $(H_2,\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_1 \rightarrow n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph_0$. Thus by maximal property of ${\mathcal P}_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$. This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ is a proper subset of ${\mathcal M}'$. This completes the proof for (i) of (e) ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ when $P=Q$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Hausdorff maximality yields a contradiction

nodes.name: Take a maximal chain
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset ${\mathcal P}_0$ of ${\mathcal P}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal chain

nodes.name: Claim: the direct sum $\pi_{max}$ is an upper bound in the chain
nodes.statement: We claim that $\pi_{max}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in ${\mathcal P}_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_1,\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists an element $(H_2,\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_1 \rightarrow n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph_0$. Thus by maximal property of ${\mathcal P}_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Claim: the direct sum $\pi_{max}$ is an upper bound in the chain

nodes.name: $\pi_{max}\in{\mathcal P}$ and chain elements have successors
nodes.statement: That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_1,\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists an element $(H_2,\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_{max}\in{\mathcal P}$ and chain elements have successors

nodes.name: Extend isometries; maximality puts $\pi_{max}$ in the chain
nodes.statement: By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_1 \rightarrow n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph_0$. Thus by maximal property of ${\mathcal P}_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Extend isometries; maximality puts $\pi_{max}$ in the chain

nodes.name: $\pi_{max}\prec\pi_{max}$ contradicts strictness
nodes.statement: This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ is a proper subset of ${\mathcal M}'$. This completes the proof for (i) of (e) ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ when $P=Q$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_{max}\prec\pi_{max}$ contradicts strictness

nodes.name: Part (f) from the proof of (e)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em In the proof of ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ in (e), we have used equality $P=Q$ just to ensure that $\Omega$ is also a cyclic for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ and $P=Q$ is used to prove $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)' = \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. So (f) follows by the proof of (e).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Part (f) from the proof of (e)

nodes.name: Part (g): tail algebra identity
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em A proof for (g) is given in [Mo3] with ${\mathcal M}_0$. Here we will also give an alternative proof relating the criteria obtained in Proposition 3.4. To that end we claim that $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)')=\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)' \bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'.$$ That $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \{ \tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J: |I|=|J| < \infty \}'$ follows by Cuntz relation and thus $\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For the reverse inclusion let $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For $n \ge 1$, we choose $|I|=n$ and set $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$. We check that it is independent of the index that we have chosen as $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_I\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_JX \tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JX\tilde{S}_J$ where in second equality we have used $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ and also $\Lambda^n(Y_n)=\sum_{|J|=n } \tilde{S}_J\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J=X$. This proves the equality in the claim. Going along the same line we also get $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)') = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'.$$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Part (g): tail algebra identity

nodes.name: Point to [Mo3]; plan alternative proof
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em A proof for (g) is given in [Mo3] with ${\mathcal M}_0$. Here we will also give an alternative proof relating the criteria obtained in Proposition 3.4.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Point to [Mo3]; plan alternative proof

nodes.name: Claim tail intersection equals joint commutant; define $Y_n$
nodes.statement: To that end we claim that $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)')=\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)' \bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'.$$ That $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \{ \tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J: |I|=|J| < \infty \}'$ follows by Cuntz relation and thus $\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For the reverse inclusion let $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For $n \ge 1$, we choose $|I|=n$ and set $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Claim tail intersection equals joint commutant; define $Y_n$

nodes.name: $Y_n$ is index independent and lifts back to $X$
nodes.statement: We check that it is independent of the index that we have chosen as $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_I\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_JX \tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JX\tilde{S}_J$ where in second equality we have used $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ and also $\Lambda^n(Y_n)=\sum_{|J|=n } \tilde{S}_J\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J=X$. This proves the equality in the claim.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $Y_n$ is index independent and lifts back to $X$

nodes.name: Same identity with ${\mathcal O}_d$
nodes.statement: Going along the same line we also get $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)') = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'.$$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Same identity with ${\mathcal O}_d$

nodes.name: Purity iff trivial tail, then duality gives the sequence criterion
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em By Proposition 3.4 $\omega$ is pure if and only if the set above is trivial. Thus once more by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] and Theorem 2.4 in [Mo2], purity is equivalent to asymptotic relation $||\psi \tilde{\tau}^n -\phi|| \rightarrow 0$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for any normal state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal M}'$ ( Here we recall by Proposition 2.4 $P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'P={\mathcal M}'$ as $P$ is also the support projection in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''{\mathcal F}$ and support projection of $\phi_{\Omega}$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ is ${\mathcal F}=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\Omega]$, where commutant is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ ). By a duality argument Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3] we conclude that $\omega$ is pure if and only if there exists a sequence of elements $x_n \in {\mathcal M}$ so that for each $m \ge 0$, $x_{m+n}\tau_n(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)1$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M} \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. This completes the proof of (d) with ${\mathcal M}$. For the proof with ${\mathcal M}_0$ we need to show if part as only if part follows ${\mathcal M}_0$ being a subset of ${\mathcal M}$ and $\tau$ takes elements of ${\mathcal M}_0$ to itself. For if part we refer to Theorem 3.2 in [Mo3].
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Purity iff trivial tail, then duality gives the sequence criterion

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant parts (M')_0
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We set $$({\mathcal M}')_0 = \{x \in {\mathcal M}' : \beta_z(x)=x,\;\; z \in H \}.$$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant parts of M-tilde and its commutant
nodes.statement: Similarly we also set $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ and $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}')_0$ as $(\beta_z:\;z \in H)$ invariant elements of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ and $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}')$ respectively.

nodes.name: Whether P lies in M-tilde^1
nodes.statement: We note that as a set $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0)'$ could be different from $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}')_0$. We note also that $P\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1P \subseteq \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ and unless $P$ is an element in $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1$, equality is not guaranteed for a factor state $\omega$. The major problem is to show that $P$ is indeed an element in $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1$ when $\omega$ is a pure state.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Dual corner set need not be an algebra
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We warn here an attentive reader that in general for a factor state $\omega$, the set ${\mathcal F} \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'' {\mathcal F}$, which is a subset of ${\mathcal F} \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'{\mathcal F}$, need not be an algebra. However by commutant lifting theorem applied to dilation $v_i \rightarrow S_i{\mathcal F}$, $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'{\mathcal F}$ is order isomorphic to ${\mathcal M}'$ as $P={\mathcal F} {\mathcal E}$ is the support projection. Thus the von-Neumann sub-algebra generated by the elements ${\mathcal F}\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''{\mathcal F}$ is order isomorphic to $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. However $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ may properly include $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_{00}=\{ P\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)P \}''$ ( as an example take $\psi$ to be the unique KMS state on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and $\omega$ be the unique trace on ${\mathcal B}$ for which we get $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_{00} = \mathbb{C}$ and $P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P$ is the linear span of $\{\tilde{v}_J^*,\;I,\;\tilde{v}_J:|J| < \infty \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: For a factor state, ${\mathcal F}\pi(\tilde{\mathcal O}_d)''{\mathcal F}$ need not be an algebra; the trace example gives a strict inclusion.

nodes.name: Modular invariance of M-tilde_0 not automatic
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Existence of a $\phi$ preserving normal conditional expectation $\int_{z \in H} \beta_z dz: {\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal M}_0$ by Proposition 2.5 ensures that modular operator of $\phi$ preserves ${\mathcal M}_0$ [Ta] and so does on $({\mathcal M}')_0$. However there is no reason to take it granted for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ to be invariant by the modular group of $(({\mathcal M}')_0,\phi)$. By Takesaki's theorem such a property is true if and only if there exists a $\phi$-invariant norm one projection from $({\mathcal M}')_0$ onto $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$. In the following we avoid this tempted route.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Relation of P=Q to purity
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em At this stage it is not clear how we can ensure existence of a normal conditional expectation from ${\mathcal M}'$ onto $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ directly and so the equality ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ when $\omega$ is a pure state. Further interesting point here that the equality $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$ holds when $\omega$ is the unique trace on ${\mathcal B}$ as $v^*_k=S^*_k$ and ${\mathcal J} \tilde{v}^*_k {\mathcal J} = {1 \over d} S_k$ for all $1 \le k \le d$ where $P \neq Q$ and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)' \supset \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. In the last proposition we have also proved if $[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]=P$ then ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Thus a natural question that arises here: how the equality $P=Q$ is related to purity of $\omega$?

nodes.name: Proof of Haag duality for translation invariant pure states
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Purity from $P=Q$ via a duality and asymptotic criterion; Haag duality by contradiction using Mackey imprimitivity and a strictly ordered set of quasi-equivalent representations. Hausdorff maximality yields an upper bound strictly above itself.

nodes.name: If part: $P$ support of the dual representation implies purity
nodes.statement: First we will prove that $\omega$ is pure if $P$ is also the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$, where $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=[\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]$. The support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and thus we also have $P = \tilde{{\mathcal E}}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ by our hypothesis. Since $\Lambda^n(P)=\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} \uparrow {\mathcal F}$ and now $\Lambda^n(P)=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}\Lambda^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \uparrow \tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, we also have ${\mathcal F} = \tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. Similarly we also have for each $n$, ${\mathcal E}\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F})=\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{{\mathcal E}})\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and thus taking limit we also get ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. \vskip 1em So we have $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}={\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}}=Q$. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}=P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P$ is cyclic in ${\mathcal K}$ i.e. $[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]=[P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P\Omega]= P\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=P{\mathcal E}=P$ as $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$. \vskip 1em However $\bigcap_{n \rightarrow \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)) = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'' \bigcap \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ ( for a proof which is a simple application of Cuntz relation, we refer to section 5 of [Mo2]). Further $\psi$ being a factor state in $K_{\omega'}$, by Proposition 3.2 $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is a factor. In particular we have $\bigcap_{n \rightarrow \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d))\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \mathbb{C} \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Thus by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] we conclude that $||\Psi \circ \tilde{\tau}_n -\phi|| \rightarrow 0$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all normal state $\Psi$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ where $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0=P \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''P$ as $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ and support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and $P={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}{\mathcal E}$. \vskip 1em Note that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0 \subseteq {\mathcal M}_0'$ where ${\mathcal M}_0=P\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''P$. Further by Proposition 2.5 ${\mathcal M}_0 = \{x \in {\mathcal M}:\beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}\;\;\;$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0=\{x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}: \beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}$. Once we set $P_0=[{\mathcal M}_0\Omega]$ then we also have $P_0=[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0\Omega]$ as $[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]=P=[{\mathcal M}\Omega]$ by expending $u_z=\sum_{k \in \hat{H}} z^kP_k$ where $z \rightarrow u_z= PU_zP$ is a unitary representation of group $H$. \vskip 1em For $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}, y \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$ we have $$\phi(\tilde{\tau}(x)y)=\sum_k <\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega,x\tilde{v}^*_ky\Omega> = \sum_k <v^*_k\Omega,x y \tilde{v}^*_k\Omega>$$ (as $v_k^*\Omega=\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega$ ) $$=\sum_k <\Omega, x v_kyv_k^* \Omega>=\phi(x \tau(y))$$ The dual group of $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}},\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given on the commutant by $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}',\tau,\phi)$ where $\tau(x)=\sum_k v_k x v_k^*$ for $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$. where commutant is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. Now moving to $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in the duality relation above, we verify that adjoint Markov map of $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0,\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given by $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0,\tau,\phi)$ where $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0$, the commutant of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}_0)$ and ${\mathcal K}_0$ is the Hilbert subspace $P_0$ with $\Omega$ as cyclic and separating vector for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ in ${\mathcal K}_0$. Thus by Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3], there exists a sequence of elements $y_n \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0$ such that for each $m \ge 1$, $y_{m+n}\tau_n(y) \rightarrow \phi(y)1$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all $y \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0 \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}_0)$. Thus $\omega$ is pure by Proposition 3.5 (e) once we recall ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ as $P=Q$ ( and so ${\mathcal M}'_0 = \tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ ) by Proposition 3.5 (d). This completes the proof of purity property of $\omega$.

nodes.statement_short: If part: $P$ support of the dual representation implies purity

nodes.name: Trivial tail and [Ar2] give asymptotic convergence of $\tilde\tau_n$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em However $\bigcap_{n \rightarrow \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)) = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'' \bigcap \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ ( for a proof which is a simple application of Cuntz relation, we refer to section 5 of [Mo2]). nodes.name: Gauge-invariant parts share the cyclic projection $P_0$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Note that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0 \subseteq {\mathcal M}_0'$ where ${\mathcal M}_0=P\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''P$. Further by Proposition 2.5 ${\mathcal M}_0 = \{x \in {\mathcal M}:\beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}\;\;\;$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0=\{x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}: \beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}$. Once we set $P_0=[{\mathcal M}_0\Omega]$ then we also have $P_0=[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0\Omega]$ as $[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]=P=[{\mathcal M}\Omega]$ by expending $u_z=\sum_{k \in \hat{H}} z^kP_k$ where $z \rightarrow u_z= PU_zP$ is a unitary representation of group $H$.

nodes.name: Duality of $\tilde\tau$ and $\tau$ with [Mo3] and Proposition 3.5 give purity
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}, y \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$ we have $$\phi(\tilde{\tau}(x)y)=\sum_k <\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega,x\tilde{v}^*_ky\Omega> = \sum_k <v^*_k\Omega,x y \tilde{v}^*_k\Omega>$$ (as $v_k^*\Omega=\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega$ ) $$=\sum_k <\Omega, x v_kyv_k^* \Omega>=\phi(x \tau(y))$$ The dual group of $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}},\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given on the commutant by $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}',\tau,\phi)$ where $\tau(x)=\sum_k v_k x v_k^*$ for $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$. where commutant is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. Now moving to $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in the duality relation above, we verify that adjoint Markov map of $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0,\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given by $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0,\tau,\phi)$ where $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0$, the commutant of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}_0)$ and ${\mathcal K}_0$ is the Hilbert subspace $P_0$ with $\Omega$ as cyclic and separating vector for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ in ${\mathcal K}_0$. Thus by Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3], there exists a sequence of elements $y_n \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0$ such that for each $m \ge 1$, $y_{m+n}\tau_n(y) \rightarrow \phi(y)1$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all $y \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0 \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}_0)$. Thus $\omega$ is pure by Proposition 3.5 (e) once we recall ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ as $P=Q$ ( and so ${\mathcal M}'_0 = \tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ ) by Proposition 3.5 (d). This completes the proof of purity property of $\omega$.

nodes.statement_short: Duality of $\tilde\tau$ and $\tau$ with [Mo3] and Proposition 3.5 give purity

nodes.name: Only-if part: purity gives $\tilde{\mathcal F}={\mathcal E}$, ${\mathcal F}=\til
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em In the following we now prove the hardest part of the theorem namely $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ and ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ if $\omega$ is pure. Proof uses extensively the general theory of quasi-equivalent representation of a $C^*$ algebra and we refer [BR1, Chapter 2.4.4] as a general reference.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Only-if part: purity gives $\tilde{\mathcal F}={\mathcal E}$, ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{\mathcal E}$

nodes.name: Shift unitary $V$ and monotone projection families
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We set unitary operator $V=\sum_k S_k\tilde{S}^*_k$. That $V$ is a unitary operator follows by Cuntz's relations and commuting property of $(S_i)$ and $(\tilde{S}_i)$. Further a simple computation shows that $V\pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$ for all $x \in {\mathcal B} = {\mathcal B}_L \otimes {\mathcal B}_R$, identified with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ and $\theta$ is the right shift. We also have \begin{equation} \theta({\mathcal E})=V {\mathcal E} V^*= \sum_{k,k'}S_k\tilde{S}^*_k {\mathcal E} S^*_{k'}\tilde{S}_{k'}=\Lambda({\mathcal E}) \ge {\mathcal E} \end{equation} Similarly we also have \begin{equation} \theta(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \ge \tilde{{\mathcal F}} \end{equation} So in particular we have $V(I-{\mathcal E})V^* \le I-{\mathcal E}$, i.e. $(I-{\mathcal E})V^*{\mathcal E}=0$. Also for any $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ we have $V^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}X\Omega = \tilde{{\mathcal F}} \sum_k \tilde{S}_k X \tilde{S}_k^*\Omega$ as $S_k^*\Omega =\tilde{S}_k^*\Omega$. Thus $(I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}})V^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=0$ i.e. $V\tilde{{\mathcal F}}V^*=\Lambda(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \ge \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Similarly we also have \begin{equation} \theta^{-1}(\tilde{{\mathcal E}})=V^*\tilde{{\mathcal E}}V \ge \tilde{{\mathcal E}}\;\mbox{and}\; V^* {\mathcal F} V \ge {\mathcal F} \end{equation} We also set two family of increasing projections for all natural numbers $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ as follows \begin{equation} {\mathcal E}_n=V^n {\mathcal E} (V^n)^*,\;\;\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_n=V^n\tilde{{\mathcal F}}(V^n)^* \end{equation}

nodes.statement_short: Shift unitary $V$ and monotone projection families

nodes.name: Powers' criterion gives weak mixing $V^n\to|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Since $\beta_z(V)=V$ for all $z \in H$, $V \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by Proposition 3.4 as $\omega$ is pure. $\omega$ being also a factor state, we have $<f,V^ng> \rightarrow <f,\Omega><\Omega,g>$ as $n \rightarrow + \mbox{or} - \infty$ for any $f,g \in \pi({\mathcal B}_{loc})\Omega$ by Power's criteria [Pow] given in (1). Since such vectors are dense in the Hilbert space topology and the family $\{V^n:n \ge 1\}$ is uniformly bounded, we get $V^n \rightarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology as $n \rightarrow + \mbox{or} - \infty$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Powers' criterion gives weak mixing $V^n\to|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|$

nodes.name: Assume $H$ trivial; split into cases
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em For the time being we assume that $H$ is trivial. Otherwise the argument that follows here we can use for the representation $\pi_0$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ i.e. $\pi$ restricted to $[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. \vskip 1em We have following distinct cases:

nodes.statement_short: Assume $H$ trivial; split into cases

nodes.name: Case 1: ${\mathcal E}\neq I$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Case 1: ${\mathcal E}\neq I$

nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Limit projection ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is trivial or infinite dimensional

nodes.name: Define ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$

nodes.name: Claim: a finite ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is $|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|$
nodes.statement: We claim that either ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty} = |\Omega><\Omega|$ or ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is a proper infinite dimensional projection i.e. if ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ is a finite projection then ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}=|\Omega><\Omega|$. Suppose not then the finite subspace is shift invariant. In particular there exists a unit vector $f$ orthogonal to $\Omega$ such that $Vf=zf$ for some $z \in S^1$ and this contradicts weak mixing property i.e. $V^n \rightarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology proved above as point spectrum of $V$ has only $1$ with spectral multiplicity $1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Claim: a finite ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is $|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|$

nodes.name: Otherwise a finite shift-invariant subspace exists
nodes.statement: Suppose not then the finite subspace is shift invariant.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise a finite shift-invariant subspace exists

nodes.name: An eigenvector contradicts weak mixing
nodes.statement: In particular there exists a unit vector $f$ orthogonal to $\Omega$ such that $Vf=zf$ for some $z \in S^1$ and this contradicts weak mixing property i.e. $V^n \rightarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology proved above as point spectrum of $V$ has only $1$ with spectral multiplicity $1$.

nodes.statement_short: An eigenvector contradicts weak mixing

nodes.name: Imprimitivity systems of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ for ${\mathcal E}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em If ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is infinite dimensional we can get a unitary operator $U_0$ from $F_0=\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ onto ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ and via the unitary map we can get a sequence of increasing projections $U_0{\mathcal E}_nU^*_0$ in ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ and note that $U_0{\mathcal E}_nU_0^*=V^nU_0 {\mathcal E} U_0^*(V^n)^*$. Note that if ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ is infinite dimension the process will not stop in finite step. Thus we have $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{{\mathcal E}}} F(k)$ where the index set is either singleton or infinity and each $F(k)$ will give a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$, where $F(1) =F_0-{\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$. Further $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ being a simple $C^*$-algebra, each such imprimitivity system is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ [Mo3,section 4]: We fix a nonzero $f \in {\mathcal E}-\theta^{-1}({\mathcal E}) \neq 0$ otherwise ${\mathcal E}=I$ as $\theta^n({\mathcal E}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. $\pi_f:x \rightarrow \theta^{-1}(x)f$ gives a representation of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d={\mathcal B}_L$ and we check that $[\pi_f(\theta^{-1}({\mathcal B}_L)''f] \le {\mathcal E}-\theta^{-1}({\mathcal E})$ as $f \perp [\theta^{-1}(\pi({\mathcal B}_R)')\Omega] \ge [\theta^{-1}(\pi({\mathcal B}_L))\Omega]$. Thus simplicity ensures that ${\mathcal E} - \theta^{-1}({\mathcal E})$ is a projection of dimension $\aleph_0$. Further $n_{\mathcal E}$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$ since $F_0$ is separable.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Imprimitivity systems of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ for ${\mathcal E}$

nodes.name: Same decomposition for $\tilde{\mathcal F}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Since $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is also a proper projection, same argument is valid for $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ with $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_{-\infty}= \mbox{lim}_{n \rightarrow -\infty} \theta^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}})$ i.e. we can write $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}} \tilde{H}(k)$, where each $\tilde{H}(k)$ give rises to a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$ where each system of imprimitivity is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ where $\tilde{F}(1) = F_0-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_{-\infty}$ and $n_{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Same decomposition for $\tilde{\mathcal F}$

nodes.name: Amplified representations $n\pi$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em In the following we use temporary notation $H$ for Hilbert subspace $F_0$. For a cardinal number $n$, we amplify a representation $\pi:{\mathcal B} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(H)$ of the $C^*$ algebra ${\mathcal B}$ to $n$ fold direct sum $n\pi=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } \pi_k $ acting on $nH=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } H_k$ defining by $$n\pi(x) (\oplus \zeta_k) = \oplus (\pi(x)\zeta_k)$$ where $\pi_k = \pi$ is the representation of ${\mathcal B}=\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ on $H_k=H$ where $H =[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. We also extend $\bar{\tilde{F}} = \oplus \tilde{F}_{\alpha}$, $\bar{E} = \oplus E_{\alpha}$ and $\bar{V}=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n} V_k$ respectively. We also set notation $\Omega_k=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}\delta^k_j\Omega$.

nodes.statement_short: Amplified representations $n\pi$

nodes.name: Mackey's theorem gives a unitary $U$ matching ${\mathcal E}$ with $\tilde{\mathc
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Thus by Mackey's theorem, there exists a cardinal number $n \in \aleph_0$ and a unitary operator $U: nH \rightarrow nH$ so that $\bar{V}=U\bar{V}U^*$ and $\bar{{\mathcal E}}=U\bar{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}U^*$. We set a representation $\pi^U:{\mathcal B} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(nH)$ by $\pi^U(x)= Un\pi(x)U^*$ and rewrite the above identity as $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^U_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$ where $\pi^U_k(x)=U\pi_k(x)U^*$. Note that by our construction we can ensure $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ for all $1 \le k \le n$ as the operator intertwining between two imprimitivity systems are acting on the orthogonal subspace of the projection generated by vectors $\{\Omega_k:1 \le k \le n\}$.

In such a case we have $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^u_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k]$$ Alternatively $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^u_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$

nodes.name: Iterating gives a strictly ordered set of quasi-equivalent representations
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Thus in principle we can repeat our construction now with $\pi^U$ and so we get a strict partial ordered set of quasi-equivalent representation of ${\mathcal B}$. In the following we now aim to employ formal set theory to bring a contradiction on our starting assumption that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}$.

nodes.name: Define the class ${\mathcal P}$ and the order with condition (C1)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em To that end we need to deal with more then one representation of ${\mathcal B}$. For the rest of the proof we reset notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ used for the pure representation of ${\mathcal B}$ in $H_0 =[\pi_0({\mathcal B})\Omega_0]$ where $\Omega_0$ is the cyclic vector, the reset notation for $\Omega$. Let ${\mathcal P}$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0:{\mathcal B} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(H_0)$ with a shift invariant vector state $\omega(x)=<\Omega,\pi(x)\Omega>$ i.e. $\omega(\pi(\theta(x))=\omega(\pi(x))$. So there exists minimal cardinal numbers $n_{\pi},n_0(\pi)$ so that $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to $n_0(\pi)\pi_0$. Thus for such an element $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega_{\pi})$ we can associate two cardinal numbers $n_{\pi}$ and $n_0(\pi)$ and without loss of generality we assume that $H_{\pi} \subseteq n_0(\pi)H_0$ and $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}=n_0(\pi)H_0.$ $\pi_0$ being a pure representation, any element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ is a type-I factor representation of ${\mathcal B}$. The interesting point here that $\displaystyle{\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P} }}\pi$ is also an element in ${\mathcal P}$ with associated cardinal numbers $\sum_{\pi} n_{\pi}$ and $\sum_{\pi} n_0(\pi)$. We say $(\pi_1,H_{\pi_1},\Omega^1) \prec (\pi_2,H_{\pi_2},\Omega^2)$ if there exists an isometry $U:n_{\pi_1} H_{\pi_1} \rightarrow n_{\pi_2} H_{\pi_2}$ so that \vskip 1em \noindent (C1) For each $1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} $ we have $U \Omega^1_{\alpha} = \Omega^2_{\alpha'}$ for some $1 \le \alpha' \le n_{\pi_2}$; \noindent

nodes.name: The order is strict and has an infinite chain
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em In the inequality we explicitly used that both Hilbert spaces are subspaces of $nH_0$ for some possibly larger cardinal number $n$. That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H,\Omega) \prec (\pi,H,\Omega)$ contradicts (C3) as $I=E_2'$. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$. Thus $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}$ and by our starting assumption that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \neq {\mathcal E}$ we also check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ there exists an element $\pi' \in {\mathcal P}$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus ${\mathcal P}_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain containing $\pi_0$.

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality contradiction: ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{\mathcal F}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset ${\mathcal P}_0$ of ${\mathcal P}$ containing $\pi_0$. We claim that $\pi_{max} = \oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in ${\mathcal P}_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists an element $(H_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_{\pi_1} \rightarrow n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph$. Thus by maximal property of ${\mathcal P}_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$. This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}$. This completes the proof that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ when ${\mathcal E} \neq I$. By symmetry of the argument we also get ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ when $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} < 1$.

Thus we get  egin{equation} 	heta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}' \end{equation} \vskip 1em We also rule out the possibility that ${\mathcal F} 	ilde{{\mathcal F}} = {\mathcal F}$. If so then ${\mathcal F} \le 	ilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \le 	ilde{\Lambda}^n(	ilde{{\mathcal F}}) = 	ilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Taking limit we get $	ilde{{\mathcal F}}=I$ as $	ilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \uparrow I$ as $n ightarrow \infty$. This brings a contradiction to our hypothesis. \vskip 1em So we have in particular ${\mathcal F}' < {\mathcal F} \le I$ and ${\mathcal F}' - |\Omega><\Omega| 
eq 0$. Now we will rule out the possibility of ${\mathcal F}=I$ under our hypothesis $	ilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$. Suppose so i.e. ${\mathcal F}=I$, then $	ilde{{\mathcal E}}=I$ since $	ilde{{\mathcal E}} \ge {\mathcal F}$. Then $Q={\mathcal E} 	ilde{{\mathcal E}} = {\mathcal E} = {\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}=P$. Thus by Proposition 3.5 (e) we get $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= \pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and so we have in particular $	ilde{{\mathcal F}}=[\pi(	ilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega]={\mathcal E}$. This contradicts our starting assumption once more that $	ilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$. \vskip 1em We also have $	heta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}'$ and $	heta^{-1}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F}$. Thus we can follow the steps of Case-1 with elements ${\mathcal F}',{\mathcal F},	heta^{-1}$ replacing the role of $	ilde{{\mathcal F}},{\mathcal E},	heta$ to get a unitary operator $U:nH ightarrow nH$ so that $U ar{V}= ar{V}U$ and $U ar{{\mathcal F}}U^*= ar{{\mathcal F}'}$ for a cardinal number $n$. \vskip 1em Now we consider a further subset ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ of ${\mathcal P}_G$ consist of quasi-equivalent representations $\pi$ to $\pi_0$ of ${\mathcal B}$ where $\pi$ admits the additional property: ${\mathcal F}_{\pi} < I, {\mathcal E}_{\pi}=I$ and $\{	heta^{-n}(	ilde{{\mathcal F}_{\pi}}): n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with ${\mathcal F}_{\pi}$ with the strict partial ordering $({\mathcal H}_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_{\pi_1}) \prec ({\mathcal H}_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_{\pi_2})$ given by modifying condition (C3') as \vskip 1em 
oindent (C3'') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] > \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$ \vskip 1em Since $\pi^U$ also satisfies the conditions that of $\pi_0 \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ by covariance relation of $U$ with respect to shifts once more we get $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus we can repeat the process and so ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ has at least one infinite chain of totally ordered containing $\pi_0$. Once more by Hausdorff maximality principle we bring a contradiction to our starting assumption that ${\mathcal F}' < {\mathcal F}$. In other words this brings a contradiction to our starting hypothesis that $	ilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is a proper projection i.e. ${\mathcal F} < {\mathcal E}=I$. Thus we arrive at $	ilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ when ${\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Sub-case $G=\tilde{\mathcal F}<I$

nodes.name: $\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})$ commutes with $\tilde{\mathcal F}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em \noindent {\bf Sub-case 2 of case 2:} Now we consider the case $G=\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < I$. In such a case we have $(1- \tilde{{\mathcal F}})\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=0$ and so $\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})$ commutes with $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ for all $n \ge 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})$ commutes with $\tilde{\mathcal F}$

nodes.name: Rule out the Bernoulli case
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em First we rule out the simplest possibility in the present situation for ${\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} = |\Omega><\Omega|$. If so then $\omega$ is a Bernoulli state and a proof follows once we compute the following using the property $\Lambda(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \ge \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}\pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and commuting property of ${\mathcal F}$ with $\pi(s_i)^*$ to get some scalars $\bar{\lambda_i}$ such that $$\bar{\lambda}_i= {\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}\pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F} = \pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F}$$ and so $$\omega(s_Is_J^*)=<\Omega,\pi(s_I) \pi(s_J)^*\Omega>$$ $$=<\Omega, {\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} \pi(s_I)\pi(s_J)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F} \Omega>$$ $$=\lambda_I\lambda_J^*$$ The inductive limit state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$, give rises to a pure state once restricted to ${\mathcal B}_R$ and thus we have ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ by Haag duality when $\pi({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a type-I factor. This contradicts our starting assumption that ${\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Rule out the Bernoulli case

nodes.name: Projection ${\mathcal F}'$ with $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}')\ge{\mathcal F}'$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we set projection ${\mathcal F}'$ defined by \begin{equation} {\mathcal F}'={\mathcal F}-{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}+|\Omega><\Omega| \end{equation} and check by commuting property of $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ with ${\mathcal F}$ that $$ {\mathcal F}'\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}'){\mathcal F}' = (I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}){\mathcal F}\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F})(I-\theta^{-1}(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}))(I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}){\mathcal F} + |\Omega><\Omega|$$ $$= {\mathcal F}(I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) + |\Omega><\Omega|={\mathcal F}'$$ where we have used $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}) = \tilde{\Lambda}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F},\; \theta({\mathcal F}) \le {\mathcal F}$ and $\theta(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) = \Lambda(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \ge \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Thus we get \begin{equation} \theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}' \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Projection ${\mathcal F}'$ with $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}')\ge{\mathcal F}'$

nodes.name: Equation (37)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal F}'={\mathcal F}-{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}+|\Omega><\Omega|
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Equation (38)
nodes.statement: \theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}'
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Rule out ${\mathcal F}\le\tilde{\mathcal F}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We also rule out the possibility that ${\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} = {\mathcal F}$. If so then ${\mathcal F} \le \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \le \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) = \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Taking limit we get $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=I$ as $\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. This brings a contradiction to our hypothesis.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Rule out ${\mathcal F}\le\tilde{\mathcal F}$

nodes.name: Rule out ${\mathcal F}=I$ via Proposition 3.5 (e)
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em So we have in particular ${\mathcal F}' < {\mathcal F} \le I$ and ${\mathcal F}' - |\Omega><\Omega| \neq 0$. Now we will rule out the possibility of ${\mathcal F}=I$ under our hypothesis $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$. Suppose so i.e. ${\mathcal F}=I$, then $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=I$ since $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \ge {\mathcal F}$. Then $Q={\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}} = {\mathcal E} = {\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}=P$. Thus by Proposition 3.5 (e) we get $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and so we have in particular $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=[\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega]={\mathcal E}$. This contradicts our starting assumption once more that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Rule out ${\mathcal F}=I$ via Proposition 3.5 (e)

nodes.name: Case-1 argument gives a unitary $U$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em We also have $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}'$ and $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F}$. Thus we can follow the steps of Case-1 with elements ${\mathcal F}',{\mathcal F},\theta^{-1}$ replacing the role of $\tilde{{\mathcal F}},{\mathcal E},\theta$ to get a unitary operator $U:nH \rightarrow nH$ so that $U\bar{V}=\bar{V}U$ and $U\bar{{\mathcal F}}U^*=\bar{{\mathcal F}'}$ for a cardinal number $n$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Case-1 argument gives a unitary $U$

nodes.name: Subclass ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ with order (C3'')
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we consider a further subset ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ of ${\mathcal P}_G$ consist of quasi-equivalent representations $\pi$ to $\pi_0$ of ${\mathcal B}$ where $\pi$ admits the additional property: ${\mathcal F}_{\pi} < I, {\mathcal E}_{\pi}=I$ and $\{\theta^{-n}(\tilde{{\mathcal F}_{\pi}}): n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with ${\mathcal F}_{\pi}$ with the strict partial ordering $({\mathcal H}_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_{\pi_1}) \prec ({\mathcal H}_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_{\pi_2})$ given by modifying condition (C3') as \vskip 1em \noindent (C3'') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] > \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Subclass ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ with order (C3'')

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality again: $\tilde{\mathcal F}={\mathcal E}$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Since $\pi^U$ also satisfies the conditions that of $\pi_0 \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ by covariance relation of $U$ with respect to shifts once more we get $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus we can repeat the process and so ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ has at least one infinite chain of totally ordered containing $\pi_0$. Once more by Hausdorff maximality principle we bring a contradiction to our starting assumption that ${\mathcal F}' < {\mathcal F}$. In other words this brings a contradiction to our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is a proper projection i.e. ${\mathcal F} < {\mathcal E}=I$. Thus we arrive at $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ when ${\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Hausdorff maximality again: $\tilde{\mathcal F}={\mathcal E}$

nodes.name: Symmetric statement; done for trivial $H$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em By symmetry of argument used here it also follows that ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ when $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=I$. This completes the proof of $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E},\;\; {\mathcal F} =\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ for the case when $H$ is the trivial closed subgroup of $S^1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric statement; done for trivial $H$

nodes.name: General $H$: reduce to the cyclic subspace via Proposition 3.4
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we will remove the assumption that $H$ is trivial using Proposition 3.4. Let $(H,\pi_0,\Omega)$ be the GNS space of the state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$. Let $e_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0$ be the support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi_0({\mathcal B}_R)''$ and $\pi_0({\mathcal B}_L)''$ respectively. Similarly we also set projections ${\mathcal F}_0=[\pi_0({\mathcal A}_R)''\Omega]$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_0=[\pi_0({\mathcal B}_L)''\Omega]$. We also set projections $q_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$ and $p_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$. \vskip 1em $\omega$ being pure, by Theorem 3.4 any $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant element of ${\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. ${\mathcal E},\tilde{{\mathcal E}},{\mathcal F}, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ are $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ elements. Thus once we identify cyclic space $[\pi_0({\mathcal B})\Omega]$ with $F_0=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$, we get obvious relations \begin{equation} {\mathcal E} F_0=e_0,\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0=\tilde{e}_0,{\mathcal F} F_0=f_0, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_0=\tilde{f}_0 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} P F_0 = p_0 \;\;\mbox{and} \;\; QF_0=q_0 \end{equation} as ${\mathcal E}=[\pi(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega]$, $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$, $Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}$. Further $V$ is also $\{ \beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant and $V \pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$ for all $x \in {\mathcal B}$ which we have identified with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$. \vskip 1em By applying the first part of the argument with representation $\pi_0$, for pure $\omega$, we have $e_0=\tilde{f}_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0=f_0$ and $p_0=q_0$. \vskip 1em Now we write the equality $p_0=q_0$ as ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} F_0={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0$ and apply $\Lambda$ on both side to conclude that $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_1=\Lambda({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_1$ and multiplying by ${\mathcal E}$ from left we get ${\mathcal E}{\mathcal F} F_1={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_1$ as $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal E}={\mathcal E}$ and thus we get $PF_1=QF_1$. By repeated application of $\Lambda$, we get $PF_m=QF_m$. \vskip 1em If $H=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ then we get $P=\sum_k PF_k=\sum_k QF_k=Q$. This completes the proof for $P=Q$. Similarly $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \sum_k \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_k = \sum_k {\mathcal E} F_k = {\mathcal E}$ and also ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. \vskip 1em If $H=S^1$ then $\hat{H}=\mathbb{Z}$ and for $m \ge 0$, we have $PF_m=QF_m$. For $m < 0$ we take $k=-m$ and check that $\Lambda^k(QF_m-PF_m)=\Lambda^k(Q)F_{m+k}-\Lambda^k(P)F_{m+k} = \Lambda^k({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_0 - \Lambda^k({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_0= \Lambda^k({\mathcal E})(\tilde{e}_0 - f_0)=0$ Since $\Lambda$ is an injective map, we get $QF_m=PF_m$ for all $m < 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: General $H$: reduce to the cyclic subspace via Proposition 3.4

nodes.name: Support and cyclic projections in the GNS space of $\omega$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we will remove the assumption that $H$ is trivial using Proposition 3.4. Let $(H,\pi_0,\Omega)$ be the GNS space of the state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$. Let $e_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0$ be the support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi_0({\mathcal B}_R)''$ and $\pi_0({\mathcal B}_L)''$ respectively. Similarly we also set projections ${\mathcal F}_0=[\pi_0({\mathcal A}_R)''\Omega]$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_0=[\pi_0({\mathcal B}_L)''\Omega]$. We also set projections $q_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$ and $p_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Support and cyclic projections in the GNS space of $\omega$

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant projections restrict to $e_0,\tilde e_0,f_0,\tilde f_0$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em $\omega$ being pure, by Theorem 3.4 any $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant element of ${\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. ${\mathcal E},\tilde{{\mathcal E}},{\mathcal F}, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ are $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ elements. Thus once we identify cyclic space $[\pi_0({\mathcal B})\Omega]$ with $F_0=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$, we get obvious relations \begin{equation} {\mathcal E} F_0=e_0,\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0=\tilde{e}_0,{\mathcal F} F_0=f_0, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_0=\tilde{f}_0 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} P F_0 = p_0 \;\;\mbox{and} \;\; QF_0=q_0 \end{equation} as ${\mathcal E}=[\pi(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega]$, $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$, $Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}$. Further $V$ is also $\{ \beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant and $V \pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$ for all $x \in {\mathcal B}$ which we have identified with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Gauge-invariant projections restrict to $e_0,\tilde e_0,f_0,\tilde f_0$

nodes.name: Equation (39)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal E} F_0=e_0,\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0=\tilde{e}_0,{\mathcal F} F_0=f_0, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_0=\tilde{f}_0
