nodes.name: Equation (40)
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Trivial-$H$ argument gives $p_0=q_0$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em By applying the first part of the argument with representation $\pi_0$, for pure $\omega$, we have $e_0=\tilde{f}_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0=f_0$ and $p_0=q_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Trivial-$H$ argument gives $p_0=q_0$

nodes.name: Apply $\Lambda$ repeatedly: $PF_m=QF_m$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we write the equality $p_0=q_0$ as ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} F_0={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0$ and apply $\Lambda$ on both side to conclude that $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_1=\Lambda({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_1$ and multiplying by ${\mathcal E}$ from left we get ${\mathcal E}{\mathcal F} F_1={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_1$ as $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal E}={\mathcal E}$ and thus we get $PF_1=QF_1$. By repeated application of $\Lambda$, we get $PF_m=QF_m$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Apply $\Lambda$ repeatedly: $PF_m=QF_m$

nodes.name: Finite $H$: sum over $F_k$ gives $P=Q$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em If $H=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ then we get $P=\sum_k PF_k=\sum_k QF_k=Q$. This completes the proof for $P=Q$. Similarly $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \sum_k \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_k = \sum_k {\mathcal E} F_k = {\mathcal E}$ and also ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Finite $H$: sum over $F_k$ gives $P=Q$

nodes.name: $H=S^1$: injectivity of $\Lambda$ handles $m<0$
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em If $H=S^1$ then $\hat{H}=\mathbb{Z}$ and for $m \ge 0$, we have $PF_m=QF_m$. For $m < 0$ we take $k=-m$ and check that $\Lambda^k(QF_m-PF_m)=\Lambda^k(Q)F_{m+k}-\Lambda^k(P)F_{m+k} = \Lambda^k({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_0 - \Lambda^k({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_0= \Lambda^k({\mathcal E})(\tilde{e}_0 - f_0)=0$ Since $\Lambda$ is an injective map, we get $QF_m=PF_m$ for all $m < 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: $H=S^1$: injectivity of $\Lambda$ handles $m<0$

nodes.name: Proposition 3.5 gives (i),(ii); gauge invariance gives Haag duality
nodes.statement: \vskip 1em Now we are left to prove those three statements given in (b). $\omega$ being pure we have $P=Q$ and thus by Proposition 3.5 we have $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$ and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. We are left to show $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'=\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$. For that we recall $F_0$ and check few obvious relation $F_0\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'F_0=F_0\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''F_0$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \subseteq F_0\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'F_0$. Since $F_0\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_0$ is equal to $(\beta_z:z \in H)$ invariant elements in $F_0\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''F_0$ and elements in $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$ are $(\beta_z: z \in H)$ invariant we conclude that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$. Inclusion in other direction is obvious and thus Haag duality property (iii) holds.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 3.5 gives (i),(ii); gauge invariance gives Haag duality

nodes.name: Proof of Purity criterion and Haag duality for translation invariant factor states
nodes.statement: (of Theorem 1.1:) (a) implies that $q_0=p_0$. (d) also says that $p_0=q_0$. Thus in either case, following last part of the proof of Theorem 3.6 we get $P=Q$. The statement (e) also implies $P=Q$. That shows now that (a),(d) as well as (e) implies (f) by the if part of Theorem 2.6 (a). That (b) implies (a) is trivial as $\Omega$ is separating for ${\mathcal M}_1,\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_1$ by faithful property. That (c) implies (f) is trivial as $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a factor. Thus we have showed so far any of the statement (a),(b),(c),(d),(e) implies (f). For the converse we appeal to the only if part of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Each statement reduces to $P=Q$, then purity via Theorem 3.6; the converse is the only-if part of Theorem 3.6.
